The card shows only while AI Insights are on, with No open insights when none are open. AI Insights are on while Turn on system-initiated AI is on and at least one insight type or background worker job is on. When AI Insights are off, the dashboard shows no insights, even ones that are still open. Click View All to open the AI Insights list.

sections.heading: Reservation Insights
sections.text:
Reservation insights describe a reservation that went wrong. They exist only while two switches are on. Reservations must be on in Settings > Integrations & Features > Reservation. Reservation insights must be on in Settings > AI > Automatic Insights. While reservations are off, EVtivity creates no reservation insights and hides the stored ones and Explain on the reservation page. They show again when you turn reservations back on.

| Insight | Known cause (rule, no tokens) | Analyzed by the AI |
|---------|-------------------------------|--------------------|
| Reservation rejected | The EVSE was occupied or in use, or the station was offline or faulted at activation | The station rejected it for another reason, or did not answer |
| Reservation no-show | Always | Never |
| Reservation cancel failed | The station was offline | The station rejected the cancellation or did not answer |
| Reservation fee failed | The payment was declined, or the driver has no payment method | The payment provider failed |
| Station faulted while reserved | Never | Always, with the station's data |

A reservation that expires because it never reached the station, because another driver used the EVSE, or because it was an operator hold without a driver is not a no-show and starts no insight.

The reservation's insights are on the AI Insights tab of the reservation page. Reservation insights do not show on the station page. Suggested fixes include Check the reserved EVSE's status, Cancel the reservation on the station again, and Review the reservation fee payment.

sections.heading: Reservation Insights
sections.text: The header of the reservation page also has Explain when the reservation was cancelled because of the station (rejected, not answered, or unavailable during the hold), when it expired, or when its fee failed. Like every Explain button, it needs the assistant turned on and the `aiAssistant:write` permission. Explain on a reservation also needs the `reservations:read` permission.

sections.heading: AI Insights List
sections.text:
Open the AI Insights list from AI Insights in the navigation. The entry shows while AI Insights are on, with the number of insight actions that wait for a decision. The list, `/ai/insights`, shows every insight of your sites, newest first. Filter by Status, Type, Root Cause, Feedback, and Site. Select Pending in the Status filter to see the insights whose action waits for a decision. The Feedback filter shows Any feedback, Marked wrong, or Marked helpful: the insights at least one user marked that way. The table has these columns: Insight, Status, Root Cause, Confidence, Station, Site, and Created.

Click a row to open the insight page, `/ai/insights/`. Prev and Next in the header move to the neighboring insight of the list. It shows:

- The insight card, with its actions (see Act on an Insight) and the suggested action, if any (see Insight Actions).
- Details: the type, station, session, and site, the site incident the insight is part of, when it was created, resolved, or dismissed, and the reason it was skipped. For an insight with an action, also the Worker job, when the action Expires, who Decided it and when, and when it ran (Ran at).
- Marked Wrong: shown when users marked the insight wrong. Each wrong vote with who gave it, when, and the note as plain text, or No note. A user your site access does not let you see shows as Another user.
- History: every change to the insight and to its action.

The Details card has an AI Insights row to stop insights where they come from:

- Suppress for This Station shows when the insight has a station. It needs the `stations:write` permission.
- Suppress for This Site shows when the insight has a site, directly or through its station. It needs the `sites:write` permission.

sections.heading: AI Insights List
sections.text:
Each button opens the suppress dialog. Enter a reason and an optional end date, and confirm. A toast confirms the change, and the insight shows as dismissed. When the station or site is already suppressed, the row shows its state instead of the button: Station suppressed until and the date, Station suppressed until resumed, Station suppressed with its site, Site suppressed until and the date, or Site suppressed until resumed. See Stations and Sites.

Each record an insight names links to its page: the station (OCPP ID), session, site (name), reservation (`#` and the reservation ID), driver (name, else email), and token. The Details card links every record, and the Station and Site columns of the list and of the station and site AI Insights tabs link theirs. Without the read permission for a record (`stations:read`, `sessions:read`, `sites:read`, `reservations:read`, or `drivers:read` for drivers and tokens), or when the record no longer exists, it shows as plain text with its ID.

Both pages need the `aiInsights:read` permission.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
- AI Insights list: open it with View All on the dashboard card, or at `/ai/insights`. Use the Status filter to see open, pending, done, rejected, resolved, dismissed, or expired insights, or All statuses.
- Insight page: the History section lists who dismissed or regenerated the insight, who set, changed, or removed a vote, who confirmed or rejected its action, how the action ended, and when.
- Audit: filter the Audit page by the Automatic Insight type, or by AI insight action for the decisions on insight actions.

You see only the insights of your sites.

sections.heading: Act on an Insight
sections.text:
These actions need the `aiInsights:write` permission:

- Regenerate: analyze again, for an insight that is out of date, resolved, not analyzed, or whose analysis did not finish. EVtivity refuses it while another analysis of the same record is running (`AI_INSIGHT_COOLDOWN`), when insights are turned off (`AI_INSIGHTS_DISABLED`), or when a budget is used up.
- Dismiss: hide an open insight you do not need.
- Helpful or Wrong: tell EVtivity whether the insight was right (see Feedback).

Ask a follow-up on the insight page and on a support case opens the AI assistant about the insight.

Dismissals and vote changes are recorded in the audit log.

sections.heading: Feedback
sections.text:
Each user has one vote per insight: Helpful or Wrong. The thumb you chose shows as pressed. Click another thumb to change your vote. Click the pressed thumb again to remove your vote: its tooltip reads Remove your vote. The vote buttons appear on every insight except one that is analyzing, not analyzed, out of date, or whose analysis did not finish.

Every reader sees how many users found the insight helpful in the card footer, such as "3 found this helpful".

When you click Wrong, the card opens a panel with Marked wrong. Generate the insight again from fresh data, or dismiss it. It holds:

- What is wrong? (optional): a note of up to 500 characters. Click Save Note to store it. Readers of the insight see it in Marked Wrong on the insight page.
- Regenerate, unless the insight is dismissed. When you typed a note without saving it, Regenerate saves it first.
- Dismiss, while the insight is open.

Votes are never sent to an AI provider. Your note is sent only when you regenerate an insight you marked wrong: the new analysis reads your own note, never the note of another user, as a claim to check against the station data, not as an instruction. EVtivity marks it as untrusted text and first masks credentials, card numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers in it. A known cause needs no AI request and ignores the note. An insight analyzed with your note shows Regenerated with your feedback. Other users see Regenerated with operator feedback. The AI assistant cannot read votes or notes. To see how insights rate over time, open the Insight Quality card in Settings > AI > Automatic Insights (see Settings).

sections.heading: Insight Actions
sections.text:
A background AI worker can suggest an action. The suggestion is an insight that carries the action:

| Insight | Action | Runs only if |
|---------|--------|--------------|
| Stuck session | Stop the session | The session is still active |
| Stuck session | End the session without the station | The session is still active |
| Station faulted for hours | Soft reset the station | The station is still faulted |

The action is the last part of the Suggested Fix section of the insight card, after the other fix steps. It shows:

- A sentence that names the action and its target, such as "Stop the charging session at station CS-1 (OCPP transaction ...)".
- Expires on and the time, on the right of the Suggested Fix heading. Hover it to see why the action expires.
- The Rationale with the measured values behind it, such as Idle Time, Last Activity, and Faulted Since, and the OCPP Transaction ID of a session.
- API Request, a collapsed panel with the method and path of the request. Open it to see the arguments.
- The result once the action ran, or the reason nothing ran.
- Reject and Confirm. After a decision, or once the action expired, the buttons stay disabled.

sections.heading: Confirm or Reject
sections.text:
1. Open the insight from AI Insights, the dashboard card, or the AI Insights tab of the station or session.
2. Read the action, the rationale, and the API request.
3. Click Confirm to run the action, or Reject to drop it.
4. Confirm your choice in the dialog. Run This Action? runs the action once, now, with your permissions. Reject This Action? drops it.

When you confirm, EVtivity checks again that the action has not expired, that the condition still holds, and that the action is still allowed. Then it runs the request with your own permissions and site access, and the result appears on the card. Each action runs at most once: when two users confirm it at the same time, only one confirm runs it. An action that expired shows `AI_PROPOSAL_EXPIRED`. An action whose condition no longer holds shows `AI_PROPOSAL_STALE`.

The decision sets the status of the insight:

| Action | Insight status |
|--------|----------------|
| Waiting for a decision | Pending |
| Confirmed and ran | Done |
| Confirmed, but did not run, for example because you lack the permission it needs | Open, with the reason on the card |
| Rejected | Rejected |
| Nobody decided before it expired | Expired |
| The condition no longer held when someone confirmed it | Resolved |

While an action waits, Regenerate and Dismiss are hidden. Click Reject to drop the action. Insights with an action cannot be regenerated.

Confirm and reject need the `aiInsights:write` permission and a signed-in CSMS session. An API key cannot decide an action (`AI_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRES_SESSION`).

A suggested soft reset expires after 24 hours by default (Action lifetime (hours)). A suggested stop expires after 2 hours.

sections.heading: Daily Digest Email
sections.text:
Users with the `aiInsights:write` permission can get a daily email with the number of insight actions that wait for a decision at their sites, per job, and a link to AI Insights filtered to Pending. The email holds counts and site names only, never AI-written text.

To turn it on, open your Profile, go to Notifications, and turn on AI insight action digest email. It is off by default. The email goes out once a day while actions are pending. Edit its template under Notifications > System Events (AI Insight Action Digest, `ai.ProposalDigest`).

sections.heading: Turn On Automatic Insights
sections.text:
1. Add an API key for a provider in Settings > AI > Providers and Keys.
2. Open Settings > AI > Automatic Insights. In the Automatic Insights and Workers card, select the Provider and turn on Turn on system-initiated AI.
3. In the Automatic Insights card, keep or turn off Station insights, Session insights, Authorization insights, and Reservation insights. All four are on by default once system-initiated AI is on. Reservation insights shows only while reservations are on.
4. Click Save.

To stop insights for one site, open the site's AI Usage tab and turn off Automatic Insights (see Sites). Only users with access to every site and the `sites:write` permission can change it.

sections.heading: Data Sent to the AI Provider
sections.text:
Automatic insights run without a user action. When system-initiated AI is on, EVtivity sends these data categories to the selected provider:

- Station data: identity, vendor, model, firmware, OCPP version, online state and heartbeat, availability and status, recent status changes, connections, boot reason, and the error codes, alerts, and information texts the station reported.
- Session data: status, stop reason, start and end times, energy, costs, currency, roaming, and payment failure reasons.
- Authorization data: the refusal outcome, the token type and state, prepaid credit, fleet credit limit state, and local list state. The token value itself is never sent: EVtivity sends a hash.
- Reservation data: status, times, cancel reason, fee state, the reservation's history entries, the reservation messages of its station (action and status only), the EVSE status changes during the hold, and the fee payment status and amounts. The driver is sent only as a hashed reference.
- Site data: counts of affected stations and sessions at the insight's site.
- Your note on a wrong vote, only when you regenerate that insight (see Feedback).

Stored credentials are removed, and card numbers, email addresses, phone numbers, and token ids are masked before anything is sent. Text a station reported is marked as untrusted, so the AI does not follow instructions in it. This data leaves your deployment. Check the provider's data retention terms before you turn automatic insights on.

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.text:
| Permission | Allows |
|------------|--------|
| `aiInsights:read` | See insights on records you can open |
| `aiInsights:write` | Regenerate, dismiss, give feedback, and confirm or reject insight actions |

By default, operators have both and viewers have `aiInsights:read`. Insights follow site access: you see only insights of your sites.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Insights never change anything on your network on their own. An insight action runs only when a user confirms it, with that user's permissions. Background workers suggest three actions today: a stop for a stuck session at an online station, an end in the CSMS for a stuck session at a station offline past the setting, and a soft reset for a station faulted for more than 6 hours. The only action kinds a worker may suggest are stop a session, end a session in the CSMS, soft reset a station, and change a station's availability. A station whose AI insights are suppressed, on its own or with its site, gets no suggestion (see Stations and Sites). Payments, pricing, and settings are never suggested.
- The card never names the AI provider or model.
- Insights are deleted after 90 days by default (Keep insights (days) in Settings > AI > Automatic Insights). An insight's action is deleted with it. Their audit entries stay after the insight is deleted.
- The API lists insights at `GET /v1/ai/insights`. See the API reference and the error codes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
EVtivity records the tokens of every AI request: assistant answers, support drafts, automatic answers to drivers, automatic insights, their translations, and background workers. Token budgets per company, per site, per user, and per driver stop AI requests once a budget is used up.

Budgets count tokens, not money, so they work the same with every provider. A request's tokens are its input tokens plus its output tokens.

sections.heading: Budgets
sections.text:
Set the budgets in the AI Limits card of Settings > AI > Usage and Limits, and the driver budget in Settings > AI > Driver Support. 0 means no limit.

| Budget | Setting | Default | Counts |
|--------|---------|---------|--------|
| Company tokens per month | `ai.budget.companyMonthlyTokens` | 0 | Every AI request |
| Tokens per site per month | `ai.budget.siteMonthlyTokens` | 0 | Requests charged to the site |
| Tokens per site per day (insights and workers) | `ai.budget.siteDailyTokens` | 300,000 | Automatic insights and background workers of the site |
| Tokens per user per day | `ai.budget.userDailyTokens` | 2,000,000 | The user's assistant and support draft requests |
| Tokens per driver per day | `ai.budget.driverDailyTokens` | 40,000 | The driver AI support requests of one driver |
| Warn at (% of a budget) | `ai.budget.warnPercent` | 80 | When to warn about the company and site monthly budgets |

- Daily budgets run from midnight to midnight UTC.
- Monthly budgets run for the calendar month in the system timezone.
- A site can have its own monthly budget. See Site Budget.

EVtivity checks the budgets before each AI request. A request that is already running finishes, so usage can go slightly over a budget.

sections.heading: Which Requests Count Where
sections.text:
| Request | Charged to |
|---------|-----------|
| Assistant and Explain | The company and the user, no site |
| Support case AI draft | The company, the user, and the site of the case's station |
| Driver AI support | The company, the site of the case's station, and the driver |
| Automatic insights and their translations | The company and the site |
| Background workers | The company and the site |
| MCP server | Nothing. MCP clients bring their own AI model |

sections.heading: When a Budget Is Used Up
sections.text:
- The assistant and support drafts show an error: `AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` for the user's daily budget, `AI_MONTHLY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` for a company or site monthly budget.
- A driver support case goes to the support team without an automatic answer. Its AI state reason is AI budget reached.
- Automatic insights are stored with their rule-based fields only, without an AI-written summary.
- Background workers store their findings and suggested actions without the AI-written text.

Users with the `settings.ai:write` permission and access to every site get an email and SMS when the company or a site reaches the warning percent of its monthly budget (AI Budget Warning) and when it uses the budget up (AI Budget Used Up), once per budget and month. A company budget at or past the warning percent also shows a banner at the top of every CSMS page. See AI Alerts.

sections.heading: Usage and Limits Tab
sections.text:
Open Settings > AI and select the Usage and Limits tab. It starts with the AI Limits card. The usage below it needs the `aiUsage:read` permission and access to every site.

- Month: a dropdown of the last 24 months. The Period shows the start and end of the month you pick.
- Company: the company's tokens this month against its budget.
- Sites: tokens per site against each site's budget, 10 sites per page.
- Assistant (not site-specific): the last row of the Sites list, tokens that belong to no site, such as assistant and Explain tokens.
- By surface: tokens per surface (Assistant, Support drafts, Driver support, Insights, Insight translations, Background workers), split into input, cached input, cache writes, output, and reasoning tokens.
- Top users: the users with the most tokens this month. Driver support tokens count in the company, site, and surface totals, but drivers are never listed or named here.

The tab shows a banner for each monthly budget at or past the warning percent. When the company or a site passes the warning percent or uses up its monthly budget, the assistant panel also shows a notice, once per budget and month.

sections.heading: Cost
sections.text: The tab shows the cost of the tokens only when the company currency is US dollars, because AI providers price in US dollars. In any other currency it shows tokens only.

sections.heading: Site Budget
sections.text:
The AI Usage tab of a site shows the AI Usage card: the site's tokens this month against its budget. The tab shows for users with the `aiUsage:read` permission, and for users with access to every site and the `sites:write` permission.

Users with access to every site and the `sites:write` permission can also change:

- Monthly token budget: leave it empty to use Tokens per site per month. 0 means no limit.
- Automatic Insights: turn off to stop automatic insights for this site.

sections.heading: Your Own Usage
sections.text: The footer of the assistant panel shows your tokens today against your daily budget, for example "Today: 12,400 of 2,000,000 tokens".

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.text:
| Permission | Allows |
|------------|--------|
| `aiUsage:read` | See company and site usage. A user limited to some sites sees only those sites, with no company totals, no assistant row, and no top users. |
| `aiAssistant:read` | See your own usage in the panel footer |

By default, operators have `aiUsage:read`.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- The API returns usage at `GET /v1/ai/usage`, `GET /v1/ai/usage/sites/{siteId}`, and `GET /v1/users/me/ai-usage`.
- See the error codes for every budget error.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Background AI workers are scheduled jobs that look for problems on your network. They find the facts with database queries, and AI only writes a short summary or rationale. A worker can suggest an action, but it cannot run one. A suggestion is an automatic insight that carries the action, with Confirm and Reject. Nothing runs until a user confirms it (see Insight Actions).

Every worker is off by default.

sections.heading: Jobs
sections.text:
| Job | Runs | What it does | Suggests |
|-----|------|--------------|----------|
| Nightly Network Summary | Daily at 05:30 | For each site with activity, compares the last 24 hours with the daily average of the 7 days before: stations online, offline, and faulted, sessions, failed sessions, refused authorizations, and alerts. Writes a short summary per site and one summary of the whole network. | A soft reset for up to 3 online stations per site that have been faulted for more than 6 hours, each as a Station faulted for hours insight |
| Stuck Sessions | Every 15 minutes | Finds active sessions that stopped reporting: no meter values or transaction events for the idle time, or on a station that is offline or a connector that reports Available, silent for 15 minutes. | At an online station, a stop of the session. At a station offline for longer than the offline time setting, an end of the session in the CSMS. Each as a Stuck session insight |
| Tariff Anomalies | Daily at 06:00 | Finds sessions billed nothing on a priced tariff, station costs that differ from the CSMS cost, prices per kWh more than 3 times the site's 30-day median, and sessions priced with an inactive tariff. | Nothing. Findings only |

Times follow the system timezone. Summaries and findings appear as automatic insights: Site summary, Network summary, and Tariff anomaly. The network summary is visible only to users with access to every site.

sections.heading: Stuck Sessions
sections.text:
- The idle time is 90 minutes by default (Idle time before a session counts as stuck (minutes)). It always stays at least 60 minutes below the stale session timeout, so a suggestion comes before the CSMS ends the session on its own.

- A session that already has a pending or rejected action gets no new suggestion.

- At an online station, the action is the same stop as Stop Session on the session page. Before it, the worker asks an OCPP 2.1 station whether it still runs the transaction. The insight then says how the stop bills the session: from its final meter reading while the station runs the transaction, or at its last metered energy when the station no longer knows it and the CSMS ends the session.

- At an offline station, the insight first advises getting the station back online: how long it has been offline, a Connection History link, and what to check (power, network or SIM, the site). When the station reconnects, it sends its stored transaction messages, so the session ends with its real final meter reading and exact billing. This insight has no action.

- Once the station has been offline for Offline time before the AI suggests ending a stuck session in the CSMS (hours) (24 hours by default), the insight suggests End Session: the CSMS closes the session without the station and bills it at its last metered energy. A later report from the station does not bill it again.

- The rationale is a fixed sentence, such as "No meter values or transaction events for 90 minutes". Turn on Write the rationale with AI to have AI write it instead. The AI rationale becomes the text of the insight. AI only explains the step the worker chose, from the measured facts; it never chooses the step.

sections.heading: Stuck Sessions
sections.text: - An action expires after 2 hours. It runs only if the session is still active and the station is still online (a stop) or still offline (an end).

sections.heading: Tariff Anomalies
sections.text: Tariff anomalies never suggest an action: changes to prices, billing, and payments are never available to AI. Review the findings and fix the tariff yourself on the Pricing page.

sections.heading: Turn On a Worker
sections.text:
1. Open Settings > AI > Automatic Insights and turn on Turn on system-initiated AI in the Automatic Insights and Workers card. Workers use the same provider and model as automatic insights.
2. In the Background AI Workers card on the same tab, turn on the jobs you want: Nightly Network Summary, Stuck Sessions, and Tariff Anomalies.
3. Optionally set Action lifetime (hours) (24 by default), the time a suggested soft reset stays open.
4. Click Save.

sections.heading: Budgets
sections.text: Each AI request of a worker counts against the site's daily token budget (Tokens per site per day (insights and workers)) and the monthly budgets. When a budget is used up, the worker still stores its findings and suggested actions, without the AI-written text. See AI Usage and Budgets.

sections.heading: Data Sent to the AI Provider
sections.text:
A worker sends the facts it found to the selected provider: per-site counts of stations, sessions, refusals, and alerts, the stuck session's station and duration, and the tariff findings. This data leaves your deployment.

What the AI Provider Receives

The AI provider never receives stored credentials, such as passwords, API keys, secrets and station passwords. Card numbers and IBANs are cut to their last 4 characters. Support drafts, automatic insights, background workers and driver support also mask email addresses and phone numbers, and hash or shorten driver token ids. The assistant sends driver contact details as stored, only to users allowed to read them. Text you type and text files you attach are checked for keys and card numbers. Images and PDFs you attach are sent as they are.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- A worker never runs an action. Only a user who confirms the action on its insight does, with that user's own permissions.
- Each job runs once per site and period, even with several worker processes.
- Users can get a daily digest email of pending insight actions.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Autocharge (charge by plugging in) starts a session for a driver without a card or the app. During the plug-in handshake (DIN 70121 or ISO 15118), a DC charger learns the vehicle id of the EV: its charging controller id (EVCCID, usually the MAC address) or its VIN. When the charger sends that id and a vehicle with Autocharge on holds it, the session starts as the vehicle's driver.

Autocharge is off by default. Turn it on company-wide under Settings > Integrations & Features > Autocharge, or for one site on the site's Details tab (Autocharge: Use Company Setting, On or Off).

sections.heading: What the Charger Sends
sections.text:
| Protocol | How the vehicle id arrives |
|----------|----------------------------|
| OCPP 2.1 | An idToken of type `MacAddress`, `EVCCID` or `VIN` |
| OCPP 2.1 | An `EVCCID` in `idToken.additionalInfo` next to a card or app start (ISO 15118-20) |
| OCPP 1.6 | The idTag carries the MAC address, often with the prefix `VID:` (for example `VID:92D50A693F80`), or the VIN |

The CSMS compares ids in one form: a MAC address in any case, with or without `:`, `-` or `.` separators, and without the `VID:` prefix; a VIN in uppercase. A card registered with the same value always wins over a vehicle.

sections.heading: Vehicle IDs on Every Session
sections.text:
Every start that carries a vehicle id stores it on the session, refused starts included:

- Sessions list: the Vehicle column shows the linked vehicle, or the id the charger sent with "(captured)".
- Session detail: the Vehicle row shows the linked vehicle, an Autocharge badge when the vehicle started the session, and the id with "Captured from the charger".
- Authorize Log: the Vehicle ID column shows the id of every start, so a refused Autocharge start is visible. The ID Token filter also finds it.

A session is linked to the driver's vehicle that holds the captured id.

sections.heading: Enrolling a Vehicle
sections.text:
A driver enrolls a vehicle in one step from a session in which a charger sent its id: in the portal session detail, Use This Vehicle for Plug-In Charging stores the id on a new or existing vehicle and turns Autocharge on. Operators do the same from the session detail with Use This Vehicle for Plug-In Charging, for the session's driver.

Operators also enter the EVCCID (MAC Address) and VIN on the vehicle (Drivers > driver > Vehicles > vehicle) and turn Autocharge on there. Autocharge needs a VIN or an EVCCID, and one vehicle at a time can use an id for Autocharge.

sections.heading: Authorization
sections.text:
A start is authorized by a vehicle when:

1. No driver token has the value.
2. A vehicle with Autocharge on holds the id.
3. Autocharge is on at the station's site.
4. The vehicle is not blocked and its driver is active.

The session then follows the same rules as a card start: payment method, pricing, the fleet credit limit and concurrent sessions. A vehicle id that is not enrolled, or a site with Autocharge off, is refused. The charger is told not to keep the authorization in its cache, so switching Autocharge off or blocking a vehicle applies to the next plug-in. Vehicles are never pushed to a station's local authorization list.

sections.heading: Notifications
sections.text: Each Autocharge start sends the driver the Autocharge Session Started notice (email and push) in place of the session started notice. It is always on: the operator switch is locked and the driver cannot turn it off. It names the vehicle and links to the portal Vehicles page, where the driver turns Autocharge off. The link needs the Driver Portal URL in Settings > Company Info.

sections.heading: Blocking a Vehicle
sections.text: On the vehicle page, Block Vehicle refuses the vehicle's VIN and EVCCID at every start, whether Autocharge is on or off, and the driver cannot turn Autocharge back on. Unblock Vehicle lifts it. Every change to a vehicle, its ids, its Autocharge switch and a block is listed on the vehicle's History tab.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Last Seen on the vehicle shows the station and time of the last session in which a charger sent its id.
- Drivers see the Autocharge switch in the portal where Autocharge is on.
- A card registered with a vehicle id as its value (token type `VIN`, `EVCCID` or `MacAddress`) keeps working as a card.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Certificates page manages the PKI (Public Key Infrastructure) for ISO 15118 Plug and Charge (PnC) and Mutual TLS station authentication. It provides a central view of CA certificates, station certificates, and certificate signing requests (CSRs).

Plug and Charge is a feature-toggled capability. Enable it in Settings > Integrations & Features > Plug & Charge before the Certificates page and related functionality become available.

sections.heading: Enable Plug and Charge
sections.text:
1. Navigate to Settings > Integrations & Features.
2. Open the Plug & Charge tab.
3. Toggle Enable Plug & Charge (ISO 15118).
4. Select a PKI provider:

| Provider | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Hubject | Hubject OPCP API with OAuth2 client credentials. Automated certificate signing via EST protocol. |
| Manual | CSRs are stored as pending. You sign them manually through the UI with your own CA. |
| Local | The CSMS issues ISO 15118 contract certificates from its own contract CA and signs station V2G certificate requests with its CPO Sub-CA. Station TLS certificate requests are signed manually as with Manual. |

5. If using Hubject, enter the OAuth2 credentials (base URL, client ID, client secret, token URL).
6. Click Test Connection to verify provider connectivity.
7. Save settings.

When PnC is disabled, the Certificates nav item is hidden and certificate-related API routes return 403.

sections.heading: Certificate Tabs
sections.text: The Certificates page has four tabs. The History tab shows only with the `audit:read` permission.

sections.heading: CA Certificates
sections.text:
Root and intermediate CA certificates used for certificate chain validation.

- Upload: Click Upload CA Certificate and paste the PEM-encoded certificate.
- Delete: Remove a CA certificate from the system.
- Refresh from Provider: Fetch root certificates from the configured PKI provider (Hubject only).

CA certificates include hash fields (issuer name hash, issuer key hash) used for OCSP status lookups.

sections.heading: Station Certificates
sections.text:
Certificates installed on charging stations for PnC (V2G) or Mutual TLS authentication.

- View certificate details: subject, issuer, serial number, expiration date, and source.
- Track certificate status: active, expiring, or expired.
- Filter by station, certificate type, or expiration status.

sections.heading: CSR Requests
sections.text:
Certificate signing requests submitted by stations via OCPP `SignCertificate`.

| CSR Status | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| Pending | CSR received, awaiting signing (Manual provider) |
| Submitted | CSR sent to PKI provider for signing (Hubject) |
| Signed | Certificate issued and sent to station |
| Rejected | CSR rejected by operator or provider |
| Expired | CSR timed out without being signed |

For the Manual provider, pending CSRs have a Sign button. Paste the signed certificate PEM to complete the signing process.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: The audit trail of certificate changes: who uploaded, deleted, signed, or rejected a certificate or CSR, and when. See Audit Logs.

sections.heading: Local Contract CA
sections.text:
With the Local provider the CSMS acts as the contract certificate provisioning service. When an EV asks its charging station for a contract (`Get15118EVCertificate`, ISO 15118-2 install or update, ISO 15118-20 install), the CSMS decodes the EXI request, checks its signature and the vehicle's OEM provisioning certificate, issues a contract certificate, encrypts its private key for the vehicle, and returns the signed EXI response.

1. In Settings > Integrations & Features > Plug & Charge, select Local Contract CA, enter the eMAID country code (2 letters) and provider ID (3 letters or digits), and save.
2. Click Create Contract CA. The CSMS generates a Mobility Operator chain and a provisioning chain for ISO 15118-2 (secp256r1) and ISO 15118-20 (secp521r1). Private keys are stored encrypted and never shown. A CA is created once. It also creates a CPO Sub-CA under the V2G root that signs the V2G certificates stations request. A CA created before it shows an Add CPO Sub-CA button.
3. Upload the OEM root certificate of each vehicle make as a CA certificate of type `OEMRootCertificate`. Requests from vehicles whose OEM provisioning certificate does not chain to an installed OEM root are refused.
4. On the driver page, create a Plug & Charge contract for the vehicle's PCID (the common name of its OEM provisioning certificate). Each contract gets a new eMAID token.

sections.heading: Local Contract CA
sections.text:
An ISO 15118-20 vehicle can install several contracts: the CSMS answers each repeated request with the next contract and the number still to come in `remainingContracts`. Revoking a contract deactivates its eMAID and reports its certificates as revoked when a station authorizes with them. The eMAID stays bound to its contract: it cannot be renamed, moved to another driver, reactivated after revocation, or deleted while the contract is active. A session started with a contract shows it in the session details.

Vehicles verify the response against the V2G root they trust. The local CA suits fleets and testing with vehicles configured to trust its V2G root. For vehicles that trust the public V2G roots, use Hubject.

To let a station trust the local CA, install the local V2G root on it (station Certificates tab, type `V2GRootCertificate`); the local contract CA lists its certificates. A contract certificate past its validity is refused with the certificate status `CertificateExpired`.

sections.heading: OCPP 1.6 Stations
sections.text: OCPP 1.6 stations run Plug and Charge as described in the Open Charge Alliance application note "Using ISO 15118 Plug & Charge with OCPP 1.6" (v1.0): the ISO 15118 messages travel in `DataTransfer` with vendor ID `org.openchargealliance.iso15118pnc`. The station sends `SignCertificate` (its V2G certificate), `Get15118EVCertificate`, `GetCertificateStatus` and `Authorize` this way, and the CSMS handles them like the OCPP 2.1 messages. The CSMS sends `CertificateSigned` for a V2G certificate, `InstallCertificate` of a V2G or MO root, `GetInstalledCertificateIds`, `DeleteCertificate` of an ISO 15118 certificate and the V2G certificate trigger the same way. The session starts with the regular `StartTransaction`, with the eMAID as ID tag, and is billed to the driver who holds the contract. The station advertises support with the configuration key `ISO15118PnCEnabled`. The application note covers ISO 15118-2 only, and the CSMS answers it only while Plug and Charge is enabled.

sections.heading: Station-Initiated
sections.text:
| OCPP Message | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| SignCertificate | Station requests a new certificate. A CSR that is not a valid PKCS#10 request is rejected. Otherwise the CSR is saved with the station's request ID and forwarded to the PKI provider. |
| Get15118EVCertificate | Station requests a contract certificate for a driver (PnC only). |
| GetCertificateStatus | Station requests OCSP status for a certificate. |
| GetCertificateChainStatus | Station requests the revocation status of the vehicle certificates (OCPP 2.1). The CSMS checks each by OCSP or by its CRL, and answers certificates of the local contract CA from its records. |

`SignCertificate` with type `ChargingStationCertificate` works regardless of the PnC toggle. This is the Mutual TLS renewal path. V2G certificate types require PnC to be enabled.

sections.heading: CSMS-Initiated
sections.text:
| OCPP Command | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| CertificateSigned | Send a signed certificate back to the station after CSR signing, with the request ID of the station's request. A certificate the station accepts is listed on its Certificates tab. |
| InstallCertificate | Install a CA certificate on a station. |
| DeleteCertificate | Remove a certificate from a station. |
| GetInstalledCertificateIds | Query which certificates are installed on a station. |

These commands are available from the station detail page Certificates tab (visible for OCPP 2.1 stations when PnC is enabled).

sections.heading: Expiration Monitoring
sections.text:
An hourly background task monitors certificate expiration:

1. Certificates within the critical window (default 7 days): triggers renewal on the station: `TriggerMessage(SignChargingStationCertificate)`, `SignV2GCertificate` or `SignV2G20Certificate` by certificate type, `ExtendedTriggerMessage(SignChargePointCertificate)` on OCPP 1.6. A renewal is not repeated while its CSR is open. Root certificates are not renewed this way.
2. Certificates within the warning window (default 30 days): generates an expiration warning event.
3. Expired certificates are marked as expired.

The station TLS certificate (Mutual TLS) is checked whether Plug and Charge is on or off. V2G certificates are checked only while Plug and Charge is enabled.

Configure warning and critical thresholds in Settings > Integrations & Features > Plug & Charge.

sections.heading: Mutual TLS Certificates
sections.text:
The Mutual TLS profile uses client certificates for station authentication. These stations present a client certificate instead of a password. The OCPP server validates the client certificate for Mutual TLS stations while allowing No Auth through TLS + Basic Auth stations to connect without one.

Mutual TLS certificate management uses the same `SignCertificate` flow with `ChargingStationCertificate` type. This path is always available and does not require the PnC toggle.

On the station detail page, Mutual TLS stations show a Security Profile badge and hide the password field. Certificate management is done through the Certificates tab.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
EVtivity includes a built-in OCPP conformance test runner based on the Open Charge Alliance OCTT (OCPP Compliance Testing Tool) specifications. The runner validates that the CSMS correctly handles OCPP protocol messages for versions 1.6, 2.0.1 and 2.1. It also tests the Charging Station Simulator against the OCTT charging station test cases for the same versions.

Tests run from the CSMS dashboard or the command line. Results are stored in the database and displayed with per-module pass/fail/skip/error counts.

Run conformance tests in a test environment, not production: a run creates temporary stations, a test driver and tokens, and changes PnC and payment settings while it runs.

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.text:
In a CSMS run, the test runner acts as a simulated charging station. It connects to the CSMS via WebSocket, sends OCPP messages, and validates the responses against the OCTT specification. In a Charging Station Simulator run, the runner acts as the CSMS. It starts a test OCPP server for each test case, connects a simulator station to it, and checks the station's messages.

1. The operator triggers a test run from the Settings page (Conformance tab) or via CLI.
2. A background worker picks up the job and runs the tests.
3. Each test connects as a provisioned station, executes its scenario, and records the result.
4. Results stream back to the UI via server-sent events in real time.

sections.heading: Test Coverage
sections.text: The conformance section lists every OCTT test case EVtivity runs, by OCPP version and module, with its current status. See OCPP Conformance Testing.

sections.heading: From the Dashboard
sections.text:
Navigate to Settings and select the Conformance tab.

1. In System Under Test, choose CSMS to test this CSMS, or Charging Station Simulator to test the simulator with the charging station test cases.
2. Choose OCPP 2.1, OCPP 2.0.1, OCPP 1.6, or Run All Tests.
3. Click Run Tests and confirm to start the run.

The run list shows the system under test of every run. A run removes its test data when it ends.

The results page shows:

- Overall pass/fail/skip/error counts
- Per-module breakdown with expandable test details
- Each test's step-by-step execution log
- Duration and error messages for failed tests

sections.heading: From the Command Line
sections.text: The command-line runner tests both the CSMS and the Charging Station Simulator, with options for TLS and OCSP tests. See Run CSMS tests from the command line.

sections.heading: Test Results
sections.text:
Each test run records:

- Run metadata - System under test, OCPP version, start/end time, total duration, triggered by user
- Per-test results - Test ID, name, module, status (passed/failed/skipped/error), duration, step details

Test statuses:

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Passed | All assertions validated successfully |
| Failed | One or more assertions did not match expected behavior |
| Skipped | Test preconditions not met or test intentionally excluded |
| Error | Test could not complete due to a connection or runtime error |

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Dashboard is the main landing page of the CSMS. It provides a comprehensive view of your charging network across three display modes: Live, Historical, and Trend. Every user sees the same dashboard. The rows you see follow your permissions:

- The financial row, the Revenue History chart and the Payment Breakdown chart need the payments permission (`payments:read`).
- The Active Sessions table needs the sessions permission (`sessions:read`).
- The OCPP ping cards need access to all sites.

sections.heading: Display Modes
sections.text: Use the mode toggle at the top of the dashboard to switch between views.

sections.heading: Live Mode
sections.text:
Live mode shows real-time data from your charging network. Stat cards display current values with day-over-day trend arrows that compare the last two snapshot days, normally yesterday and the day before. This avoids comparing an incomplete current day against a full previous day.

Trend arrows use color coding:

| Arrow Color | Meaning |
|-------------|---------|
| Green | Positive change (or negative for metrics where lower is better, like latency) |
| Red | Negative change (or positive for metrics where lower is better) |
| Gray | No change |

Hover (or tap on mobile) a trend arrow to see the exact percentage and the two dates it compares (e.g., "+2.5% (3/12 vs 3/11)").

Trend arrows are suppressed when either of the two days has no snapshot data. On the first 1-2 days after a fresh deployment, the earlier snapshot does not exist yet, so the cards render without arrows instead of showing a misleading +100% vs an empty baseline. The snapshot endpoint surfaces a `hasData` flag the frontend uses to make this decision.

Live updates refresh the numbers as stations and sessions change. Today's numbers are live. All-time totals can take up to a minute to reflect a change to an older record, for example a refund on an old session.

sections.heading: Historical Mode
sections.text:
Historical mode displays snapshot data for a selected date or date range. Use the date picker to choose a specific day or a range. The picker's earliest selectable date is the oldest snapshot date on record, so you can't pick pre-history dates that would only render a `No Data` overlay. Snapshots are collected daily by a background worker job and stored per site.

When you select a date range, values are aggregated across days. Percentages like uptime use weighted averages based on station count.

The snapshot endpoint returns a `hasData` flag the dashboard uses to decide whether to show the snapshot stat cards or fall back to the live cards under a No Data overlay. Snapshots are populated by a nightly background worker. Each run also fills any missing day of the last week, so a missed run leaves no gap. A brand-new deployment will not have a snapshot for yesterday until the worker has run at least once.

sections.heading: Trend Mode
sections.text: Trend mode shows 14-day sparkline charts for each metric. Each stat card displays a mini chart and the percentage change over the 14-day period.

sections.heading: Stat Cards
sections.text:
The dashboard displays three rows of stat cards.

Station Health: Total stations, online percentage, active sessions, energy delivered, faulted stations, total ports. Total Stations and the online percentage count accepted stations. Pending and blocked stations (see Onboarding Status) show as a small note under Total Stations.

OCPP and Infrastructure: Connected stations, uptime percentage over the last 30 days, average ping latency, ping success rate. The ping cards show only to users with access to all sites.

Financials: Total Revenue (incl. tax) and Today's Revenue (incl. tax), transaction count, Revenue/Session, Total Revenue (excl. tax), Total Tax Collected, total electricity cost, and Total Profit, each with a today value. This row shows only to users with the payments permission. Electricity cost and profit are populated from the per-site electricity rate periods configured on each site's Electricity Rates tab. See Sites for how to configure rate periods.

sections.heading: Card States
sections.text: Every card and chart shows a loading state while its data loads, an error with a Retry button when the data fails to load, or an empty state when there is no data. A card never shows a zero or 100% for data that did not load.

sections.heading: Revenue
sections.text:
Revenue counts money actually charged, in the company currency:

- The final cost of ended sessions, minus refunds.
- Reservation cancellation and no-show fees charged, minus refunds.
- Active sessions are not counted. Their running cost is an estimate until the session ends.

Revenue includes tax. Every session stores its net amount and tax with its cost, per tariff segment and tax rate, so Total Revenue (excl. tax) reads the stored split instead of recomputing it. A partly refunded session and each reservation fee are split at their own tax rate. Total Tax Collected is the tax that revenue contains. Tax is owed to the tax authority, so profit is computed from revenue excluding tax:

```
profit = revenue (excl. tax) - electricity cost
```

Profit can be negative. Today's values count sessions started today and fees charged today. Sessions billed in an earlier company currency are left out of revenue totals.

Revenue/Session divides the revenue of billed sessions by the number of billed sessions. Reservation fees are left out. Live and historical mode use the same definition.

Profit counts only sessions with an electricity cost. To find the sessions it leaves out, select Missing in the electricity cost filter of the sessions list. See Electricity Rates and Recalculate Electricity Cost. Profit also leaves out the electricity cost of unpaid account (fleet) sessions until their invoice is paid.

sections.heading: Active Insights
sections.text:
The Active Insights card shows below the stat cards, full width. It shows the open and pending automatic insights of your sites as cards in a row that scrolls sideways: three in view on wide screens, two on medium screens, and one on phones. Dots below the row show the scroll position. Click a dot to scroll to it. Site incidents come first. Click a card to open the insight, or View All to open the AI Insights list.

The card needs the `aiInsights:read` permission and shows only while AI Insights are on, with No open insights when none are open. When AI Insights are off, the dashboard shows no insights, even ones that are still open. See Active Insights Card.

sections.heading: Charts
sections.text:
The dashboard includes these chart panels:

- Station Status - Connector status distribution across your network (available, occupied, charging, faulted, etc.)
- Utilization - Per-site utilization over a date range, measured per charging port in service. It never exceeds 100%.
- Energy History - Energy delivered over time
- Session History - Session count over time
- Revenue History - Revenue over time, by the same definition as the revenue cards (payments permission)
- Payment Breakdown - Payment status distribution (captured, pending, failed, refunded) (payments permission)
- Peak Usage - Heatmap showing sessions by hour and day of week
- Site Map - Geographic map of your site locations

sections.heading: Chart Date Ranges
sections.text:
Chart date ranges are whole calendar days in the system timezone. Days without data show as zero.

The chart date pickers (energy, sessions, revenue, peak usage, utilization) constrain the start input to `max = end` and the end input to `min = start`, so the UI cannot produce an inverted range. The API mirrors the rule on its side: a zero or negative day count, an invalid custom `from` or `to` date, `from > to`, a range longer than 90 days, or a `from` date in the future gets a `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` instead of silently receiving last-7-days data.

sections.heading: Active Sessions
sections.text: Users with the sessions permission see the Active Sessions table with real-time updates.

sections.heading: CO₂ Avoided
sections.text: When carbon regions are configured on your sites, the dashboard displays a CO₂ Avoided stat card showing the total carbon offset from EV charging sessions.

sections.heading: Data Filtering
sections.text: All dashboard data is filtered by your site access permissions. If you have access to specific sites only, the dashboard shows data for those sites. Users with full site access see network-wide aggregations.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Display messages push pricing information and custom text to station screens using the OCPP 2.1 `SetDisplayMessage` command. Manage messages per station from the Station Detail page.

Display messages require OCPP 2.1. Stations running OCPP 1.6 do not support this feature.

sections.heading: Managing Messages
sections.text:
Operators can perform three actions from the Station Detail page:

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Create and send | Compose a message with text, priority, state, and optional transaction or component targeting, then send it to the station |
| Clear | Remove an accepted message from the station |
| Refresh | Query the station via `GetDisplayMessages` to update the message list |

sections.heading: Offline Stations
sections.text: Send Message and Refresh from Station need a connected station. Clear Message (the trash icon of an accepted message) also works while the station is offline: the CSMS queues the clear and shows "Station offline. The command is queued and sent when the station reconnects." The message keeps its status until the station reconnects and answers. An accepted clear then marks it cleared. The same happens when a station disconnects while a message is being sent or refreshed.

sections.heading: Message Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Text | The message content displayed on the station screen |
| Priority | Message priority level |
| State | Display state (e.g., charging, idle) |
| Transaction ID | Optional - target a specific transaction |
| Component | Optional - target a specific station component |

sections.heading: Status Lifecycle
sections.text:
Each display message has a status that tracks its lifecycle:

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| pending | Sent to the station but not yet confirmed |
| accepted | Station confirmed receipt and will display the message |
| rejected | Station refused the message |
| unknown | Status could not be determined |

sections.heading: Automated Pricing Messages
sections.text:
The CSMS can push pricing and status messages to all connected OCPP 2.1 stations automatically (OCPP 1.6 stations get the Idle screen as a vendor `DataTransfer`). Turn on Enable Station Messages (`stationMessage.enabled`) under Settings > Integrations & Features > Messages. Prices follow the company price display and the display language. See Station display messages.

When enabled, stations display current pricing information without manual operator intervention.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Drivers are EV owners who charge at your stations. Each driver has an account with authentication tokens, vehicles, payment methods, and notification preferences. Drivers can self-register through the portal or be created by operators in the CSMS.

sections.heading: Create a Driver
sections.text:
1. Navigate to Drivers in the sidebar.
2. Click Create Driver.
3. Enter the driver's name, email, and phone number.
4. Optionally set the driver's language. The portal, notifications, and invoice PDFs use it.
5. Click Create.

sections.heading: Driver Detail
sections.text:
Click any driver in the list to open the detail page. The default Details view edits the driver's name, email, phone, and language.

Clear the email or phone field to remove it. A driver with portal access keeps an email address, because they sign in with it. Changing the email cancels any open invitation, password reset, and email verification link sent to the old address. The new address counts as unverified: a driver with portal access gets a verification link at the new address and can still sign in. A change of letter case only keeps the address verified.

sections.heading: Tokens
sections.text: View and manage the driver's authentication tokens. Add new RFID cards or app-based tokens. Toggle tokens between active and inactive. See Tokens for more details on token types and management.

sections.heading: Payment Methods
sections.text:
View the driver's saved payment methods (credit/debit cards stored by the payment provider). Shows the card brand, last four digits, Provider (Stripe, Adyen, or Test provider), and the default card. Drivers manage their cards in the portal and the mobile app.

Operators can also add a card for a driver with Create Payment Method, set the default with Set as default, and delete a card. The card form is the active provider's. When the card issuer asks for 3D Secure with Adyen, the issuer's page opens, and the browser returns to the dashboard's `/payments/return` page, which saves the card and goes back to the driver.

sections.heading: Vehicles
sections.text: View the driver's registered vehicles. Vehicles are used to estimate miles driven based on energy consumed and the vehicle's efficiency rating. The system includes a lookup table of common EV models with their mi/kWh efficiency values.

sections.heading: Sessions
sections.text: View all charging sessions for this driver with the same filters available on the main sessions list.

sections.heading: Invoices
sections.text:
Monthly invoices for the driver's charging sessions. Click Generate Invoice to aggregate the driver's completed, uninvoiced sessions over a date range into one invoice. The invoice has one line per session and tax rate, plus one line for each reservation cancellation or no-show fee charged in the range. Statuses: draft, issued, paid, void, credited. An invoice is created as paid when every session on it was already charged in full to the driver's card or prepaid balance (or cost nothing), and as issued when an amount is still open. Sessions billed to a fleet (charge on account) are left out: the fleet invoice bills them. See Fleets. When the fleet invoices each member, the tab also lists the driver's member invoices, each with a "Via" badge that names the fleet. See Member Invoices.

Click an invoice number to open the detail page, which shows the billed driver, line items linked to their sessions, and totals. From there you can print, download, or resend the invoice, mark it paid, or issue a credit note. Only a draft invoice can be voided.

Mark paid and credit notes

An issued invoice is never changed. You record a payment or correct the invoice with these actions on the detail page (both need the `payments:write` permission):

sections.heading: Invoices
sections.text:
- Mark Paid records money received outside EVtivity, such as a bank transfer, on an issued invoice. Enter the Payment date and, optionally, the Payment reference. The invoice moves to paid.
- Issue Credit Note cancels an issued or paid invoice in full. Enter the Reason. The credit note has its own number (`CN-YYYYMM-NNNN`), lists every line of the invoice with negative amounts, and names the invoice it credits. The invoice keeps its content and moves to credited, and its sessions can be invoiced again with the correct amounts. Reservation fees on it are not invoiced again. When the invoice was paid, refund the money outside EVtivity; the credit note says so. The driver gets the Credit Note Issued notification. An invoice can be credited once.

Only a draft invoice can be voided. EVtivity creates no draft invoices, so correct every issued invoice with a credit note. This follows the German GoBD rules for electronic records. The invoice history shows who marked an invoice paid or credited it.

The History section at the bottom of the detail page lists every change made to the invoice, with who made it and when. It starts collapsed. Click it to open it. It needs the `audit:read` permission and does not print.

Invoice and credit note numbers have no gaps: a number is used only when the invoice is saved. The running number (NNNN) continues across months and does not restart each month.

Amounts and tax

Invoice amounts are stated net, with the tax per rate, as EU invoices require:

- Line items - description, quantity, net unit price, Tax Rate, and Net Amount. The note "Unit prices and amounts exclude tax." appears below the table.
- Totals - Subtotal (net), Total Tax, and the total.
- Tax Summary - one row per tax rate with Tax Rate, Net Amount, Tax, and Gross Amount.

sections.heading: Invoices
sections.text:
The total always equals what the driver was charged. Invoices read the net amount and tax each session stored with its final cost, so a later tariff change never alters an invoice. Tax is rounded to the cent per session, as the driver was billed, so the tax of a rate can differ by a cent per session from the rate applied to the summed net amount.

A session billed across tariffs with split billing gets one line per tax rate, so tariffs with different rates are invoiced separately and still add up to the amount charged.

Language and PDF

Download produces a PDF in the driver's language (English, German, Spanish, Korean, Simplified Chinese, or Traditional Chinese), the language the driver chose in the portal or you set on the driver. Invoices without a driver render in English. Korean and Chinese PDFs use the Noto Sans CJK fonts installed in the API Docker image. Outside Docker (for example `npm run dev:api` on macOS) the fonts are missing, and those invoices render in English.

Every invoice and credit note PDF shows the PDF logo at the top and the PDF footer centered at the bottom of each page, as set in Settings. The "From" block shows the company name and address and the invoice seller details: tax ID, registration number, and invoice contact. Empty fields are left out.

sections.heading: Authorize Log
sections.text: Cross-token forensic view filtered to this driver: every OCPP Authorize attempt the CSMS has seen where the matched driver is this one. Useful for diagnosing why a specific driver's card was rejected (blocked / expired / concurrent_tx / no_credit) regardless of which of their cards was tapped. Same underlying data as the global /tokens/authorize-log page.

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.text: Assign a driver-specific pricing group. Driver-level pricing takes the highest priority in the tariff resolution chain, applying at all stations regardless of station or site pricing. See Pricing for the full priority system.

sections.heading: Driver Portal Access
sections.text:
Drivers you create in the CSMS have no portal password. The Driver Portal Access card on the Details view shows whether the driver can sign in to the portal:

- Active: the driver has a password and signs in like any self-registered driver. They reset it from the portal sign-in page.
- Invited: an invitation is open. The card shows when it expires.
- Not invited: the driver cannot sign in to the portal.

To give the driver portal access on their existing account:

1. Open the driver and confirm the email address is correct.
2. Click Invite to Driver Portal, then Send Invite.
3. The driver receives an email with a link to set a password. The link works once and expires after 7 days.

The driver keeps their sessions, tokens, payment methods, and invoices. If the link expires or the email is lost, click Resend Invite. Each new invitation replaces the earlier link. The button is disabled for an inactive driver or one without an email address, and needs the `drivers:write` permission.

A driver without a password cannot register a new account with the same email, sign in, or request a password reset. Only an invitation from the operator sets the first password, so knowing a driver's email is not enough to take over the account. Edit the email text on the Notifications page under the Driver Portal Invite event.

sections.heading: Billing Address
sections.text:
The Billing Address card on the Details view holds the bill-to block of the invoices a fleet addresses to this driver. See Member Invoices.

1. Click Edit on the card.
2. Enter Name on Invoice, Street, City, State or Region, Postal Code and Country. Leave Name on Invoice empty to use the driver's first and last name. An empty field clears the stored value.
3. Click Save.

Drivers edit the same address in the portal and the mobile app. Editing it needs the `drivers:write` permission, and each change is recorded in the driver history with the fields that changed.

A driver without a billing address shows "No billing address. Invoices show the name and email." A missing address never blocks an invoice. The fleet's Driver Invoices table marks the driver with a No Address badge, and the portal and the app ask the driver to add one.

sections.heading: Deactivating or Deleting a Driver
sections.text:
Deactivating a driver (toggling Active off on the Details tab) blocks the account from new charging activity but preserves all historical sessions, tokens, and audit rows. `DELETE /v1/drivers/:id` in the API performs a soft delete with the same effect: the driver is marked inactive, not removed.

Both actions deactivate every active RFID card or app token of the driver, because charging stations are authorized by the token's own status, not the driver's. Without this a deactivated driver could still charge by tapping a card issued earlier. Both actions also sign the driver out of the driver portal and the mobile app, and cancel any open invitation, password reset, and email verification link. An inactive driver cannot get a new token.

Reactivating the driver does not auto-reactivate the tokens. Tokens may have been deliberately revoked (stolen card, lost fob) before the driver was deactivated, and reactivating them blindly would override that intent. Reactivate individual tokens from the Tokens page after reactivating the driver.

sections.heading: Erasing a Driver's Personal Data
sections.text:
To honor a request to erase personal data (GDPR right to erasure), open the driver and click Erase Driver on the Details tab. Type the driver ID to confirm. The action cannot be undone and needs the `drivers:write` permission and access to every site.

The erasure removes the driver's name, email, phone, billing address, password, MFA, notification preferences, vehicles and saved payment methods (detached from the payment provider), and deactivates the tokens. The driver can no longer sign in. Sessions, payments, invoices and credit notes stay for accounting with the details they were issued with, and earlier audit entries are kept. The page then shows Erased Driver, and the driver can no longer be edited.

A driver with an active charging session cannot be erased until the session ends.

sections.heading: Email Uniqueness
sections.text: Driver emails are case-insensitive and globally unique. `Alice@example.com` and `alice@example.com` are the same address, and only one driver row can hold either form. The CSMS normalizes email to lowercase on create and update. A duplicate returns `409 DUPLICATE_EMAIL`.

sections.heading: Timezone
sections.text: The timezone field accepts any IANA timezone name (`America/New_York`, `Europe/Berlin`, `Asia/Tokyo`). Unknown values are rejected with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Firmware campaigns let you update charging station firmware across your network. Create a campaign targeting specific stations by site, vendor, model, or station, then track per-station progress as the update rolls out.

sections.heading: Campaign Lifecycle
sections.text:
Firmware campaigns follow a draft-to-completion lifecycle:

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Draft | Campaign created but not started. You can edit the target filter, the firmware URL, the download and install settings, and the signing fields. |
| Active | Campaign started. OCPP `UpdateFirmware` commands sent to the matching online stations. Matching stations that are offline get the update when they connect. |
| Completed | All target stations have finished (installed or failed). |
| Cancelled | Campaign stopped before completion. |

sections.heading: Create a Firmware Campaign
sections.text:
1. Navigate to Settings and open the Firmware Campaign tab.
2. Click Create.
3. Fill in the campaign details:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Name | Descriptive name for the campaign (e.g., "ABB v3.2.1 Rollout") |
| Firmware URL | HTTPS URL where stations download the firmware file |
| Version | Target firmware version string (optional, for tracking) |
| Download Retries | How often a station retries a failed download, from 0 to 100. 0 means no retries. Empty lets the station decide. |
| Retry Interval (Seconds) | Seconds between download retries, from 1 to 86400. Empty lets the station decide. |
| Install Time | When the station installs the firmware. It downloads first and installs at this time. Must be in the future. Empty installs right after the download. |
| Signing Certificate (PEM) | Firmware Signing certificate for a signed update. See Signed Firmware Updates. |
| Firmware Signature (base64) | Signature of the firmware file. Set together with the signing certificate. |

Leave both signing fields empty for an unsigned update. See Download Retries and Install Time for how each OCPP version receives these settings.

sections.heading: Set Target Filter
sections.text:
Define which stations receive the update:

- Site: Target all stations at a specific site.
- Vendor: Filter by station vendor/manufacturer.
- Model: Filter by station model.
- Station: Target one station.

Filters can be combined. Leave them empty to target all stations. The Matching Stations tab lists every matching station, online and offline. Through the API, `targetFilter.firmwareVersion` also limits the campaign to stations that run that firmware version.

sections.heading: Start the Campaign
sections.text:
1. Open the campaign detail page.
2. Review the list of matching stations.
3. Click Start Campaign.
4. The system sends OCPP `UpdateFirmware` commands to each matching online station.
5. Each matching station that is offline gets the same update the next time it connects. The CSMS sends it once per station, also when the station reconnects several times.

The campaign status changes from Draft to Active.

sections.heading: Track Progress
sections.text:
Each station in the campaign progresses through these statuses:

| Station Status | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| Pending | The station has not reported yet, or it is offline and gets the update when it connects |
| Downloading | Station is downloading the firmware file |
| Downloaded | Download complete (and signature verified), awaiting installation |
| Installing | Station is installing the firmware or rebooting to install it |
| Installed | Firmware update completed |
| Failed | Update failed or never started (check error info for details) |

The campaign detail page shows a summary of station statuses and a per-station breakdown. Station status updates arrive via OCPP `FirmwareStatusNotification` messages from the stations. Installed and Failed are final: a late or repeated status report does not change them.

When all stations reach a terminal state (installed or failed), the campaign status changes to Completed. A station that never connects keeps the campaign Active. Cancel the campaign to stop waiting for it.

Cancelling cannot stop an update a station already received, because OCPP has no firmware cancel. Updates still queued for an offline station are dropped: they are never sent, and their stations show Failed.

sections.heading: Updates a Station Never Starts
sections.text:
Some updates end before the station downloads anything. The station row shows Failed with the reason as error info, and the station's Firmware Updates tab shows the update as `Rejected` with the same reason:

| Reason | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `Rejected` | The station refused the update. |
| `InvalidCertificate` | The signing certificate is not valid for the station. See Signature Failures. |
| `RevokedCertificate` | The signing certificate was revoked. |
| `CommandFailed` | The station answered the command with an error, or the CSMS could not send it. |
| `QueueExpired` | The station went offline before the command reached it and stayed offline until the queued command expired. |
| `AcceptedCanceled` | A newer firmware update replaced this one on the station, so this one never finishes. |

The campaign completes once every other station has finished.

sections.heading: Download Retries and Install Time
sections.text:
The campaign sends the same settings to every station:

| OCPP Version | Download Retries and Retry Interval | Install Time |
|--------------|-------------------------------------|--------------|
| 2.1 | `retries` and `retryInterval` in `UpdateFirmware` | `firmware.installDateTime` |
| 1.6 signed update | `retries` and `retryInterval` in `SignedUpdateFirmware` | `firmware.installDateTime` |
| 1.6 unsigned update | `retries` and `retryInterval` in `UpdateFirmware` | Not supported: the station installs right after the download |

A station with an install time reports `InstallScheduled` after the download and installs at that time. The campaign shows the station as Downloaded until it installs.

sections.heading: Signed Firmware Updates
sections.text:
A signed (secure) firmware update lets the station confirm that the firmware comes from its manufacturer before it installs it. You send the manufacturer's Firmware Signing certificate and the firmware signature with the download URL. The station checks the certificate, downloads the file, verifies the signature, and installs the firmware only when both checks pass.

OCPP 2.1 requires the CSMS to include the signing certificate in every `UpdateFirmware` request (L01.FR.11). Many OCPP 2.1 stations reject an update without it, and the EVtivity simulator does. Get the signing certificate and the signature from your station manufacturer with each firmware release.

sections.heading: Send a Signed Update
sections.text:
- Campaign: fill in Signing Certificate (PEM) and Firmware Signature (base64) when you create the campaign, or edit them while the campaign is a draft. The campaign detail page shows Signature as Signed or Unsigned. Every station in the campaign gets the same certificate and signature.
- Single station: open the station detail page, go to the OCPP Commands tab, and choose Update Firmware. Enter the Firmware Location URL, the Retrieve Date/Time, and the two signing fields.

sections.heading: OCPP Messages
sections.text:
| OCPP Version | Signed Update | Unsigned Update | Status Reports |
|--------------|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| 2.1 | `UpdateFirmware` with `firmware.signingCertificate` and `firmware.signature` | `UpdateFirmware` without the signing fields | `FirmwareStatusNotification` |
| 1.6 | `SignedUpdateFirmware` (OCPP 1.6 Security Whitepaper) | `UpdateFirmware` (`location`, `retrieveDate`) | `SignedFirmwareStatusNotification` for a signed update, `FirmwareStatusNotification` for an unsigned one |

You do not pick the message. The CSMS sends `SignedUpdateFirmware` to an OCPP 1.6 station when both signing fields are set, and the plain `UpdateFirmware` when they are empty. The CSMS records the status reports in the station's Firmware Updates tab and in the campaign.

sections.heading: Certificate and Signature Requirements
sections.text:
The CSMS checks the fields before it sends the update and returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` when one fails:

| Field | Requirement |
|-------|-------------|
| Signing certificate | One PEM encoded X.509 certificate (`-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` to `-----END CERTIFICATE-----`) that parses as X.509. At most 5500 characters. |
| Firmware signature | Base64 encoded, at most 800 characters. |
| Both | Set together or both empty. |

The station checks the rest:

- A manufacturer root certificate installed on the station (certificate type `ManufacturerRootCertificate`) must issue the signing certificate. The OCPP specification does not allow intermediate certificates for firmware signing, so the manufacturer root issues the signing certificate directly.
- The signing certificate must be valid (not expired).
- The signature must match the downloaded file and the signing certificate's key.

Stations usually ship with the manufacturer root certificate. To install one on an OCPP 2.1 station, use Install Certificate on the station Certificates tab (shown when Plug and Charge is enabled) or the `InstallCertificate` command on the OCPP Commands tab. For an OCPP 1.6 station, use the API endpoint `POST /v1/ocpp/commands/v16/InstallCertificate`. Without a manufacturer root certificate, a station cannot install signed firmware.

sections.heading: Signature Failures
sections.text:
| Station Result | Meaning |
|----------------|---------|
| `InvalidCertificate` response | The signing certificate does not chain to an installed manufacturer root, or it expired. The station does not download the firmware and reports the security event `InvalidFirmwareSigningCertificate`. The campaign marks the station Failed. |
| `InvalidSignature` status | The downloaded file does not match the signature. The station does not install it and reports the security event `InvalidFirmwareSignature`. |
| `SignatureVerified` status | The signature is valid. Installation follows. |

An `InvalidSignature` status marks the station faulted, the same as any failed install (see Considerations).

sections.heading: Considerations
sections.text:
- Online stations get the update when the campaign starts. Offline stations stay Pending until they connect.
- Firmware updates may cause stations to reboot. Active charging sessions could be interrupted.
- While a station installs firmware, its status is unavailable and drivers cannot start charging.
- A failed install (`InstallationFailed`, `InvalidSignature`, or `InstallVerificationFailed`) marks the station faulted. It stays faulted after a reboot. The next install clears it, or an operator clicks Enable Station on the station detail page.
- The firmware URL must be accessible from the station's network. The station downloads the file. The CSMS never fetches it.
- OCPP 1.6, 2.0.1 and 2.1 stations are supported. Command translation handles version differences.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Fleets group drivers, stations, and vehicles under a single organizational entity. Use fleets to manage corporate charging programs, municipal vehicle fleets, or any scenario where a group of drivers shares pricing or station access.

sections.heading: Create a Fleet
sections.text:
