EVtivity compares the station's current configuration against the most recently pushed template and flags any variable whose value no longer matches. For an OCPP 2.0.1 station, a template variable that OCPP 2.0.1 does not define and the station never reported does not count as drift. You can re-push the template to bring drifted stations back into compliance.

sections.heading: Station Detail: Configurations
sections.text:
Individual station configuration is visible on the station detail page under the Configurations tab. This is where you read or push configuration to a single station rather than an entire fleet slice.

- View: read-only table of every variable the station is reporting, sourced from the most recent `NotifyReport` (2.1) or `GetConfiguration` response (1.6).
- Refresh from Station: re-issue the read so the table reflects the latest station state. The CSMS sends `GetBaseReport` (2.1) or `GetConfiguration` (1.6) and updates the table when the station replies. The screenshot above shows the table after a refresh has populated it from the live station.
- Push Configuration: push a single template to this one station. Useful for ad-hoc tuning or testing a template against one station before rolling it out fleet-wide. Clicking the button opens a dialog where you choose a template that matches the station's OCPP version.

After a successful push, the same auto-refresh runs so the table immediately reflects the new values.

Instanced Variables

OCPP 2.1 components and variables can have an instance name. The table keeps one row per component, component instance, variable, variable instance, EVSE, connector, and attribute type. For example, `DeviceDataCtrlr.ItemsPerMessage` has the instances `GetReport` and `GetVariables`, and the table shows them as two rows with their own values. The CSMS splits large `GetVariables` requests by the `ItemsPerMessage[GetVariables]` value, and drift detection compares the top-level `Actual` row a template sets.

sections.heading: How It Compares to Adjacent Features
sections.text:
Configuration management is one of three independent OCPP write paths in the CSMS. Don't confuse them.

| Feature | OCPP Command | What It Changes |
|---------|--------------|-----------------|
| Station Configurations | `SetVariables` / `ChangeConfiguration` | Operating parameters (auth, timers, intervals, vendor flags) |
| Smart Charging | `SetChargingProfile` | Power delivery schedules |
| Firmware Campaigns | `UpdateFirmware` | Station software image |

A station can have all three pushed at once. They don't interact at the protocol level, and each tracks its own pushes.

sections.heading: Reference Pages
sections.text:
- OCPP 1.6 Configuration Keys - flat key reference
- OCPP 2.1 Components & Variables - hierarchical reference

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
OCPP 1.6 configuration is a flat list of named keys. Each key is read with `GetConfiguration` and written with `ChangeConfiguration`. The standard defines roughly 50 keys across nine functional areas. Vendors are free to add their own keys; those are not covered here.

A few protocol facts to keep in mind:

- All values travel as strings on the wire, regardless of underlying type.
- `ChangeConfiguration` returns one of `Accepted`, `Rejected`, `RebootRequired`, or `NotSupported`.
- A station only has to support keys for the features it actually implements. Reading an unsupported key returns it in the `unknownKey` array.

The tables below group standard keys by the OCPP 1.6 feature profile they belong to.

sections.heading: Core Profile
sections.text:
The Core profile is mandatory. Every OCPP 1.6 station supports these keys.

| Key | Type | Mutability | Reboot | Purpose |

|-----|------|------------|--------|---------|

| `AllowOfflineTxForUnknownId` | boolean | RW | No | Allow transactions for unknown ID tags while offline |

| `AuthorizationCacheEnabled` | boolean | RW | No | Cache authorization responses locally for offline use |

| `AuthorizeRemoteTxRequests` | boolean | R or RW | No | Authorize tokens from `RemoteStartTransaction` against backend |

| `BlinkRepeat` | integer | RW | No | Number of times Light should blink for `Light` state |

| `ClockAlignedDataInterval` | integer (s) | RW | No | Period for clock-aligned `MeterValues` (0 disables) |

| `ConnectionTimeOut` | integer (s) | RW | No | Time after authorization to start the transaction before unlock |

| `ConnectorPhaseRotation` | CSL | RW | No | Phase rotation per connector (e.g. `RST`, `RTS`) |

| `ConnectorPhaseRotationMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max number of items in `ConnectorPhaseRotation` list |

| `GetConfigurationMaxKeys` | integer | R | - | Max keys allowed in a single `GetConfiguration` request |

| `HeartbeatInterval` | integer (s) | RW | No | Heartbeat send interval |

| `LightIntensity` | integer (%) | RW | No | Percentage of max intensity for the indicator light |

| `LocalAuthorizeOffline` | boolean | RW | No | Authorize against the local list while offline |

| `LocalPreAuthorize` | boolean | RW | No | Authorize against the local list even while online (skip backend) |

| `MaxEnergyOnInvalidId` | integer (Wh) | RW | No | Max energy delivered if the ID becomes invalid mid-charge |

| `MeterValuesAlignedData` | CSL of measurands | RW | No | Measurands sampled at the clock-aligned interval |

sections.heading: Core Profile
sections.text:
| `MeterValuesAlignedDataMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max measurands in `MeterValuesAlignedData` |

| `MeterValuesSampledData` | CSL of measurands | RW | No | Measurands sampled during a transaction |

| `MeterValuesSampledDataMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max measurands in `MeterValuesSampledData` |

| `MeterValueSampleInterval` | integer (s) | RW | No | Period for transaction-related `MeterValues` (0 disables) |

| `MinimumStatusDuration` | integer (s) | RW | No | Min time a status must persist before reporting |

| `NumberOfConnectors` | integer | R | - | Number of physical connectors on the station |

| `ResetRetries` | integer | RW | No | Number of times a soft `Reset` is retried before hard reset |

| `StopTransactionOnEVSideDisconnect` | boolean | RW | No | Stop the transaction when the EV is unplugged |

| `StopTransactionOnInvalidId` | boolean | RW | No | Stop the transaction when the ID becomes invalid |

| `StopTxnAlignedData` | CSL of measurands | RW | No | Measurands sampled when a transaction stops at clock alignment |

| `StopTxnAlignedDataMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max measurands in `StopTxnAlignedData` |

| `StopTxnSampledData` | CSL of measurands | RW | No | Measurands sampled when a transaction stops |

| `StopTxnSampledDataMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max measurands in `StopTxnSampledData` |

| `SupportedFeatureProfiles` | CSL of strings | R | - | Profiles the station supports (Core, FirmwareManagement, etc.) |

| `SupportedFeatureProfilesMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max items in `SupportedFeatureProfiles` |

| `TransactionMessageAttempts` | integer | RW | No | Retries for `StartTransaction` / `StopTransaction` on failure |

| `TransactionMessageRetryInterval` | integer (s) | RW | No | Wait between transaction message retries |

sections.heading: Core Profile
sections.text:
| `UnlockConnectorOnEVSideDisconnect` | boolean | RW | No | Unlock the cable when the EV is disconnected |

| `WebSocketPingInterval` | integer (s) | RW | No | WebSocket ping interval (security stack) |

sections.heading: Local Authorization List Profile
sections.text:
Optional. Lets the station authorize tokens locally without backend roundtrip.

| Key | Type | Mutability | Reboot | Purpose |
|-----|------|------------|--------|---------|
| `LocalAuthListEnabled` | boolean | RW | No | Master switch for the local authorization list |
| `LocalAuthListMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max number of entries in the list |
| `SendLocalListMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max entries in a single `SendLocalList` request |

sections.heading: Smart Charging Profile
sections.text:
Optional. Required for any operator that wants to set power schedules.

| Key | Type | Mutability | Reboot | Purpose |
|-----|------|------------|--------|---------|
| `ChargeProfileMaxStackLevel` | integer | R | - | Max `stackLevel` accepted in a charging profile |
| `ChargingScheduleAllowedChargingRateUnit` | CSL | R | - | `Current`, `Power`, or both |
| `ChargingScheduleMaxPeriods` | integer | R | - | Max periods per charging schedule |
| `ConnectorSwitch3to1PhaseSupported` | boolean | R | - | Whether the station can switch between 3-phase and 1-phase mid-charge |
| `MaxChargingProfilesInstalled` | integer | R | - | Max profiles the station will store at once |

sections.heading: Reservation Profile
sections.text:
Optional.

| Key | Type | Mutability | Reboot | Purpose |
|-----|------|------------|--------|---------|
| `ReserveConnectorZeroSupported` | boolean | R | - | Whether the station accepts reservations for connector ID 0 (any) |

sections.heading: Security (Security Profile 1, 2, 3)
sections.text:
Optional, defined in OCPP Security Whitepaper. Configures Basic Auth, TLS, and certificate handling.

| Key | Type | Mutability | Reboot | Purpose |
|-----|------|------------|--------|---------|
| `AuthorizationKey` | string | WO | Yes | Basic Auth password for the station, hex-encoded (16-20 byte password, at most 40 hex characters). Set by the CSMS when you change or rotate the password. Templates and the generic `ChangeConfiguration` command cannot set it. |
| `CertificateSignedMaxChainSize` | integer | R | - | Max bytes of a signed certificate chain |
| `CertificateStoreMaxLength` | integer | R | - | Max number of installed certificates |
| `CpoName` | string | RW | No | CPO name embedded in CSRs |
| `SecurityProfile` | integer | RW | Yes | 0 (none), 1 (basic auth), 2 (basic auth + TLS), 3 (mutual TLS). Can only be increased. The CSMS sets it and resets the station when you upgrade the profile. |
| `AdditionalRootCertificateCheck` | boolean | R | - | Whether the station validates server cert against an additional root |

sections.heading: Notes on Mutability
sections.text:
- R (ReadOnly): Read with `GetConfiguration`, can't be written.
- RW (ReadWrite): Read and write.
- WO (WriteOnly): Write with `ChangeConfiguration`. Reads return the key in `unknownKey` to avoid leaking secrets like `AuthorizationKey`.

sections.heading: Reboot Required
sections.text: Many keys take effect immediately. A few - notably `SecurityProfile`, `AuthorizationKey`, certificate store changes, and most timing parameters on some vendors - require a station reboot. The station signals this by returning `RebootRequired` from `ChangeConfiguration`. The new value is staged and applied on the next boot.

sections.heading: Vendor Keys
sections.text:
OCPP 1.6 lets vendors add custom keys. Common patterns:

- `WebSocketPingInterval` is standard, but `WebSocketKeepAliveInterval` (vendor-specific) appears on some stations.
- Free-vending stations expose vendor keys like `FreeCharging`, `FreeVendEnabled`, or `FreeModeActive` because OCPP 1.6 has no standard way to disable authorization.
- Display brightness, badge reader timing, and language selection are almost always vendor keys.

EVtivity treats vendor keys the same as standard keys - you list them in a template and push. The CSMS doesn't validate the key name against a whitelist, so a typo will surface as a `Rejected` from the station rather than a CSMS error.

sections.heading: See Also
sections.text:
- Station Configurations overview
- OCPP 2.1 Components & Variables

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
OCPP 2.1 replaces 1.6's flat key list with a hierarchical model: a station has _components_, components expose _variables_, and each variable carries up to four typed _attributes_ (`Actual`, `Target`, `MinSet`, `MaxSet`). Configuration is read with `GetVariables` (point) or `GetBaseReport` (full inventory) and written with `SetVariables`.

Stations describe their own configuration shape: a `NotifyReport` from the station enumerates every component, variable, attribute, data type, mutability, and constraint. A CSMS can validate writes against that schema rather than guessing.

A few protocol facts to keep in mind:

- Components can be _instanced_ per EVSE or per connector via `evse.id` and `evse.connectorId`. Station-wide components leave both fields unset.
- Each variable has a `dataType` (`boolean`, `integer`, `decimal`, `string`, `dateTime`, `OptionList`, `SequenceList`, `MemberList`).
- Each variable has a `mutability`: `ReadOnly`, `WriteOnly`, or `ReadWrite`.
- `SetVariables` returns a per-variable status (`Accepted`, `Rejected`, `RebootRequired`, `NotSupported`, `UnknownComponent`, `UnknownVariable`).

The catalog below covers the standard components and the variables most operators actually touch. The full list runs to several hundred variables; the OCPP 2.1 specification is the authoritative reference.

sections.heading: Authorization (AuthCtrlr)
sections.text:
Master controls for how the station authorizes tokens.

| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch for authorization (free-vending sets this to `false`) |
| `AdditionalInfoItemsPerMessage` | integer | RW | Max entries in `additionalInfo` per `AuthorizeRequest` |
| `AuthorizeRemoteStart` | boolean | RW | Authorize tokens from `RequestStartTransaction` against backend |
| `LocalAuthorizeOffline` | boolean | RW | Authorize against local list while offline |
| `LocalPreAuthorize` | boolean | RW | Skip backend authorization when token is in local list |
| `MasterPassGroupId` | string | RW | Token group permitted to stop transactions started by other tokens |
| `OfflineTxForUnknownIdEnabled` | boolean | RW | Allow transactions for unknown tokens while offline |
| `DisableRemoteAuthorization` | boolean | RW | Reject all `RequestStartTransaction` from CSMS |

sections.heading: Transaction Control (TxCtrlr)
sections.text:
When transactions start, when they stop, and timeouts.

| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `EVConnectionTimeOut` | integer (s) | RW | Time after authorization before unlock if no EV plugs in |
| `MaxEnergyOnInvalidId` | integer (Wh) | RW | Energy ceiling when the ID becomes invalid mid-charge |
| `StopTxOnEVSideDisconnect` | boolean | RW | Stop transaction when EV is unplugged |
| `StopTxOnInvalidId` | boolean | RW | Stop transaction when the ID becomes invalid |
| `TxStartPoint` | SequenceList | RW | Events that start a transaction (`PowerPathClosed`, `EVConnected`, `Authorized`, etc.) |
| `TxStopPoint` | SequenceList | RW | Events that stop a transaction |

sections.heading: Sampled Data (SampledDataCtrlr)
sections.text:
What the station samples on its meter and when.

| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch for sampled data |
| `TxStartedMeasurands` | MemberList | RW | Measurands sampled at transaction start |
| `TxUpdatedMeasurands` | MemberList | RW | Measurands sampled during a transaction |
| `TxUpdatedInterval` | integer (s) | RW | Period between in-transaction samples |
| `TxEndedMeasurands` | MemberList | RW | Measurands sampled when a transaction ends |
| `TxEndedInterval` | integer (s) | RW | If non-zero, batches end-of-transaction samples at this interval |

Common measurands: `Energy.Active.Import.Register`, `Power.Active.Import`, `Current.Import`, `Voltage`, `SoC`, `Temperature`, `Frequency`.

sections.heading: Aligned Data (AlignedDataCtrlr)
sections.text:
Clock-aligned meter values (independent of transactions).

| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch for clock-aligned sampling |
| `Interval` | integer (s) | RW | Alignment interval (e.g. 900 = on the quarter hour) |
| `Measurands` | MemberList | RW | Measurands sampled at each alignment |
| `SendDuringIdle` | boolean | RW | Send aligned samples even when no transaction is active |

sections.heading: OCPP Communications Controller (OCPPCommCtrlr)
sections.text:
CSMS communication parameters.

| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `HeartbeatInterval` | integer (s) | RW | Heartbeat send interval |
| `MessageAttempts` | integer | RW | Retries on transaction message failure |
| `MessageAttemptInterval` | integer (s) | RW | Wait between retries |
| `MessageTimeout` | integer (s) | RW | OCPP message response timeout |
| `WebSocketPingInterval` | integer (s) | RW | WebSocket ping interval |
| `OfflineThreshold` | integer (s) | RW | Time without successful CSMS contact before declaring offline |
| `ResetRetries` | integer | RW | Soft-reset retries before hard reset |
| `NetworkConfigurationPriority` | SequenceList | RW | Order in which network profiles are tried |

sections.heading: Reservation (ReservationCtrlr)
sections.text:
| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch for reservations |
| `NonEvseSpecific` | boolean | R | Whether reservations can target the station rather than a specific EVSE |

sections.heading: Smart Charging (SmartChargingCtrlr)

Tariff-aware power scheduling.

| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch for `SetChargingProfile` |
| `ACPhaseSwitchingSupported` | boolean | R | Whether the station can switch between 1-phase and 3-phase mid-charge |
| `EntriesChargingProfiles` | integer | R | Max charging profiles installed at once |
| `LimitChangeSignificance` | decimal | RW | Min change (kW) before the station notifies the CSMS |
| `PeriodsPerSchedule` | integer | R | Max periods per charging schedule |
| `ProfileStackLevel` | integer | R | Max stack level supported |
| `RateUnit` | MemberList | R | `A`, `W`, or both |

sections.heading: Display Messages (DisplayMessageCtrlr)
sections.text:
| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch |
| `NumberOfDisplayMessages` | integer | R | Max messages stored at once |
| `PersonalMessageSize` | integer | R | Max length of a single message |

In-session pricing display.

|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `TariffEnabled` | boolean | RW | Whether the station displays tariff information |
| `CostEnabled` | boolean | RW | Whether the station displays running cost |
| `Currency` | string (ISO 4217) | RW | Currency for displayed amounts |

sections.heading: Local Authorization List (LocalAuthListCtrlr)
sections.text:
| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |

| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch |
| `Entries` | integer | R | Current entry count |
| `ItemsPerMessage` | integer | R | Max entries per `SendLocalList` message |
| `Storage` | integer | R | Max entries the station can store |

sections.heading: Authorization Cache (AuthCacheCtrlr)
sections.text:
| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch |

sections.heading: Security Controller (SecurityCtrlr)
sections.text:
| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `BasicAuthPassword` | string | WO | Basic Auth password (returned write-only to avoid leaking). Set by the CSMS when you change or rotate the password. Templates and the generic `SetVariables` command cannot set it. |
| `CertificateEntries` | integer | R | Number of installed certificates |
| `Identity` | string | RW | Station's identity string used in Basic Auth |
| `OrganizationName` | string | RW | Used in CSRs |
| `SecurityProfile` | integer | R | 0, 1, 2, or 3. Read-only. The CSMS changes it with a new network connection profile (`SetNetworkProfile`) and `OCPPCommCtrlr.NetworkConfigurationPriority`. |
| `AdditionalRootCertificateCheck` | boolean | R | Validates server cert against an additional root |

sections.text:
Required for Plug & Charge support.

| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Enabled` | boolean | RW | Master switch for ISO 15118 |
| `CentralContractValidationAllowed` | boolean | RW | Allow CSMS to validate contract certificates |
| `ContractValidationOffline` | boolean | RW | Allow station to validate contract certificates while offline |
| `RequestMeteringReceipt` | boolean | RW | Request signed metering receipts from the EV |

sections.heading: Connector / EVSE Components
sections.text: These are component _instances_ - one per physical part - with their own variables.

sections.heading: EVSE (per EVSE)
sections.text:
| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Available` | boolean | RW | Whether the EVSE is operational |
| `AvailabilityState` | OptionList | R | Current availability status |
| `Power` | decimal (W) | R | Current power being delivered |
| `SupplyPhases` | integer | R | Number of supply phases (1 or 3) |
| `AllowReset` | boolean | R | Whether `Reset` is supported on this EVSE |

sections.heading: Connector (per connector)
sections.text:
| Variable | Type | Mutability | Purpose |
|----------|------|------------|---------|
| `Available` | boolean | RW | Whether the connector is operational |
| `AvailabilityState` | OptionList | R | Current availability |
| `ConnectorType` | OptionList | R | `cType1`, `cType2`, `cCCS1`, `cCCS2`, `cCHAdeMO`, `cTesla`, etc. |
| `SupplyPhases` | integer | R | Phases on this connector |

sections.heading: Mutability Cheat Sheet
sections.text:
- R (ReadOnly): Read with `GetVariables`, write returns `Rejected`.
- RW (ReadWrite): Read and write.
- WO (WriteOnly): Write only. Reads return the variable in the `unknown` array (avoids leaking secrets like `BasicAuthPassword`).

sections.heading: Per-EVSE Scope
sections.text:
Component instances let you configure differently per EVSE. For example:

- `SampledDataCtrlr.TxUpdatedInterval` set station-wide to 60s, but on EVSE 1 set to 10s for a high-priority customer
- `Connector.Available = false` to take a single connector out of service while the rest of the station keeps running

The CSMS encodes this via `evse.id` and `evse.connectorId` in `SetVariables`. EVtivity templates support per-EVSE values when authoring the component path.

sections.heading: Vendor Variables
sections.text: Stations are free to expose custom components and variables. They appear in `NotifyReport` like any other variable, and EVtivity will read and write them. Custom variables don't go through the standard schema validation, so the CSMS surfaces a `Rejected` if the station refuses the value.

sections.heading: See Also
sections.text:

- OCPP 1.6 Configuration Keys

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
The Connectivity tab on the Station Detail page shows how a cellular station connects: what the SIM provider reports about its SIM, what the station's modem reports about its signal, and a timeline of the station's OCPP connects and disconnects beside its cellular data sessions and SIM alerts.

The tab and the ICCID field on the Details tab show only while a SIM provider or Read Signal from Stations is on. Both are off by default. See SIM Providers for the settings.

Opening the tab fetches nothing: it shows what was stored by the last Refresh.

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.text:
| Action | Needs |
|---|---|
| Open the tab, Refresh, Look Up Again | `stations:read` and access to the station's site |
| Confirm SIM | `stations:write` and access to every site |
| Reset Network, Clear Match, Read Device Model, editing the ICCID | `stations:write` and access to the station's site |

sections.heading: SIM matching
sections.text:
The CSMS finds a station's SIM from its ICCID. The station reports it when it boots, or you enter it on the Details tab (19 or 20 digits, a 19-digit ICCID may end in F, with an optional IMSI of up to 15 digits). A station that reports another ICCID when it boots replaces the entered one.

On the first Refresh, the CSMS asks each enabled provider for the ICCID and stores the first match. When no provider knows the ICCID, the tab says so and the CSMS does not ask again for an hour. Look Up Again asks at once.

Changing the ICCID, on the Details tab or by the station at boot, removes the match. Clear Match removes it by hand. The next Refresh looks the SIM up again. The station History tab records each match, confirmation and removal with the provider name, never the ICCID.

sections.heading: Confirm SIM
sections.text:
Nothing is fetched for a match until it is confirmed: no SIM status, sessions or alerts, and no network reset. A match is confirmed when:

- a user with access to every site entered the ICCID on the Details tab, or
- a user with `stations:write` and access to every site clicks Confirm SIM.

A match made from the ICCID the station reported, or from an ICCID a user with access to some sites only entered, stays unconfirmed until Confirm SIM. So a station that reports a SIM it does not hold, or a user limited to some sites, cannot make a SIM a reset target.

The dialog shows the ICCID, the provider and where the ICCID came from: reported by the station, or entered by a named user. Confirm SIM is refused when:

- another station already holds a confirmed match for the same SIM (`409 SIM_CONFIRMED_ELSEWHERE`). A SIM serves one station only.
- the match changed after the dialog opened, for example the station reported another ICCID (`409 SIM_MATCH_CHANGED`). Nothing is confirmed and the tab reloads, so you can check the new match first.

A lookup that finds a SIM another station holds as confirmed shows that the SIM is matched to another station, and this station shows no SIM data.

sections.heading: Refresh
sections.text:
The SIM and Signal Data card has one Refresh control. One click reads the SIM provider and, while Read Signal from Stations is on, the station. Each part reports its own result line, such as the number of sessions and alerts stored or why it was skipped.

1. Pick a Period: the last 1, 3, 7, 14 or 31 days, or the default period from the settings (7 days unless changed). Periods longer than the provider keeps data (Hologram: 90 days) or than the CSMS keeps it are disabled, with the reason below the select.
2. Or click Custom Range and pick up to 31 days within that window. Days count in the time zone of the station's site, else the system time zone, and the range cannot end in the future. The dialog shows what is already stored for the chosen days.
3. Click Refresh.

The provider part reads the SIM status, then the data sessions and SIM alerts of the period. A period overlapping one fetched before stores each session and alert once. The station part sends one OCPP request: `GetVariables` of the modem (`DataLink`) variables for OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1, `GetConfiguration` of the configured keys for OCPP 1.6. It runs at most once a minute per station and is skipped for an offline station. The station read uses a small amount of the station's cellular data when the station connects over cellular.

A station can be refreshed 6 times a minute. More answers `429 SIM_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED` and the tab shows how long to wait.

sections.heading: From the Provider
sections.text:
The card shows the SIM as the provider reported it at the last Refresh:

- Provider, State (Active, Pending, Suspended, Inactive, Deactivated, Test or Unknown, with the provider's own state name)
- In Session: whether a data session is open, and since when
- Network with its radio access technology (for example LTE), Cell ID, APN, Profile
- Last Session and Data This Period, with the end of the billing period
- a warning when the SIM used more than 80 percent of the data limit the provider reports. The provider may pause it at the limit.
- Recent SIM Alerts: the five newest stored alerts

Fields the provider does not report are named under the card. SIM alerts arrive only with a Refresh: a data limit pause shows after the next Refresh.

sections.heading: From the Station
sections.text:
While Read Signal from Stations is on, the card shows what the station's modem reported at the last Refresh, per modem:

- Signal Strength with its unit and grade. A value in ASU is shown with its dBm value.
- In Use, Enabled, Fallback Link, Problem Reported, Network Address, ICCID, IMSI and Network Profile Slot, when the station reports them.

An OCPP 2.0.1 or 2.1 station that has not reported its modem yet shows Read Device Model. It asks the station for its full device model (`GetBaseReport`). Click Refresh a minute later. For an OCPP 1.6 station the card lists the configuration keys named in the settings as the station reported them.

sections.heading: Signal grade
sections.text: The grade is Good at or above the good threshold (default -65 dBm), Fair at or above the fair threshold (default -85 dBm) and Poor below. These are RSSI thresholds. OCPP does not say which measure a modem reports, so an LTE modem that reports RSRP reads 20 to 30 dB lower and grades lower than its link. The info icon next to the grade says the same.

sections.heading: Timeline
sections.text:
Pick a Range (Last Hour, Last 24 Hours, Last 7 Days, Last 31 Days or a custom range). The timeline lists, newest first:

- OCPP Connected and Disconnected
- SIM Data Session with its end, data, network and cell
- SIM alerts: Data Limit Reached, Data Warning, Moved to Another Device, Device Model Changed, First Device
- Low Signal and Signal Restored, from the low signal alert

The note above the timeline says when SIM data was last fetched and that the provider reports a data session only after it closes (Hologram: up to 6 hours later).

sections.heading: Data coverage
sections.text:
A strip of days shows what is stored for each day:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Has Data | Fetched, with sessions |
| No Sessions | Fetched, without sessions |
| Partly Fetched | Part of the day was fetched |
| Pending | Within the provider's reporting delay |
| Not Fetched | No Refresh covered the day |
| No Longer Available | Older than the provider's history or the CSMS retention |

Click a Not Fetched or Partly Fetched day to open the custom range for it. Runs of days that were not fetched show as one timeline row with Fetch.

sections.heading: Likely cause of a disconnect
sections.text:
Each Disconnected row shows a likely cause, worked out from stored data when the timeline is read. A disconnect never calls the provider.

| Label | When | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| Likely Cause: CSMS | The CSMS restarted, or one of its processes stopped | The station reconnects on its own. Check the CSMS if it did not. |
| Likely Cause: SIM Account | A data limit alert was stored for the SIM from 24 hours before to 1 hour after the disconnect | The SIM's data plan at the provider |
| Likely Cause: Station | The cellular data session was open across the disconnect | The station and its connection to the CSMS |
| Likely Cause: Cellular Network | Within a fetched period, the SIM had no data session at that time | The cellular coverage at the site and the station's antenna |
| Cause Pending | The provider has not reported that time yet | Click Refresh after the reporting delay |
| Cause Unknown | No SIM data is stored for that time | A Refresh that covers that day may tell more |

sections.heading: Reset Network
sections.text:
Reset Network asks the provider to end the station's data session, and the station reconnects to the cellular network. The station can be offline until it reconnects. Click Refresh after a few minutes to see the new session.

- It needs a confirmed match. Before Confirm SIM the button is disabled (`409 SIM_MATCH_NOT_CONFIRMED` through the API).
- It shows only when the provider supports a network reset.
- One reset per station a minute. A second one answers `429 SIM_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED` with the time to wait.
- The station History tab records each reset (command `SimNetworkReset`) with its outcome.

sections.heading: Error codes
sections.text: The SIM routes answer with the `SIM_*` codes listed under Sites & Stations in the error code reference.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Station images allow operators to upload, tag, and manage photos for each station. Access this feature from the Images tab on the Station Detail page.

sections.heading: Upload
sections.text: Upload images via presigned S3 URLs. Maximum file size is 10MB per image.

sections.heading: Main Image
sections.text: Set one image as the main image. The main image displays in the station header across the CSMS.

sections.heading: Tags and Captions
sections.text: Add tags and captions to organize images. Tags help filter and categorize photos across stations.

sections.heading: Driver Visibility
sections.text: Mark images as driver-visible to show them on the Portal Location Detail page. Drivers see these images when browsing station locations.

sections.heading: Reorder
sections.text: Reorder images via drag-and-drop or bulk reorder. The display order determines how images appear in the station detail view.

sections.heading: Full-Screen Viewer
sections.text: View any image in a full-screen viewer for detailed inspection.

sections.heading: Storage
sections.text:
Images are stored in S3 with the key format:

```bash
stations/{stationId}/{uuid}-{fileName}
```

This uses the same S3 configuration as support case attachments.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Stations represent physical charging hardware that communicates with the CSMS over OCPP 1.6, 2.0.1 or 2.1. Each station has one or more EVSEs (Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment), and each EVSE has one or more connectors. The CSMS manages the full lifecycle: registration, real-time monitoring, configuration, security, and certificate management.

sections.heading: Create a Station
sections.text:
1. Navigate to Stations in the sidebar.
2. Click Create Station.
3. Enter the station ID (must match the identity the station uses when connecting via OCPP).
4. Select the OCPP protocol version (1.6, 2.0.1 or 2.1). It must match the version the station offers when it connects. See OCPP Settings for what OCPP 2.0.1 stations do not support.
5. Assign a site, vendor, and model.
6. Set the security profile (No Auth through Mutual TLS).
7. Add EVSEs and connectors with their power ratings and connector types.
8. Click Create.

Each new station gets an empty configuration template bound to it, also when the station comes from a site CSV import.

sections.heading: Onboarding Status
sections.text:
New stations start with a pending onboarding status. Operators can approve or block stations from the station detail page.

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| pending | Awaiting operator approval. Station can connect via OCPP but cannot start charging sessions. |
| accepted | Approved and fully operational. |
| blocked | Rejected or suspended by operator. Station cannot connect via OCPP at all. |

sections.heading: Connection behavior
sections.text:
- Pending stations are allowed to connect over OCPP so operators can send configuration commands during onboarding. Charging is blocked at the API level (remote start requests are refused).
- Blocked stations are rejected at the WebSocket connection level. The station cannot connect, send messages, or receive commands.
- Accepted stations connect and operate normally.

sections.heading: Approving and blocking
sections.text:
- To approve a pending station, click Approve on the station detail page. A connected station is asked to boot again at once.
- To block a pending station, click Reject and confirm. The station's OCPP connection is terminated immediately.
- To unblock a blocked station, click Unblock. This sets the status back to pending. The station can reconnect but still requires approval before it can start charging sessions.

sections.heading: Deleting a station
sections.text:
Stations cannot be permanently deleted. The Delete button blocks the station instead of deleting it from the database and closes its OCPP connection. This preserves all historical data (sessions, meter values, logs). You can unblock it later to restore it to pending status. While a charging session is active at the station, Delete is refused with `409 STATION_HAS_ACTIVE_SESSION`: stop the session first (Connectors tab, Stop Active Session).

Approve, Reject, Unblock and Delete need the `stations:write` permission. Without it, the station page shows the onboarding notice without the buttons.

sections.heading: Station Status
sections.text:
The station list, the station detail page, the site Stations and Layout tabs, and the fleet Stations tab show one status per station. Station-level conditions come first. Otherwise the status summarizes the connectors in this order: charging, reserved, faulted, unknown, available, unavailable.

Hover the status badge to see why a station is unavailable or faulted. The Status row on the Details tab shows the same reason.

| Reason | Status | Cause |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Disabled by an operator | unavailable | An operator clicked Disable Station |
| Disabled after a critical security event | unavailable | The station sent a critical `SecurityEventNotification` |
| Firmware install failed | faulted | The last firmware install failed |
| The station reports a fault | faulted | The station reported `Faulted` for itself |
| A connector reports a fault | faulted | At least one connector is faulted |
| Installing firmware | unavailable | A firmware install is in progress |
| The station reports itself unavailable | unavailable | The station reported `Unavailable` for itself |

sections.heading: How availability is computed
sections.text:
The CSMS computes each station's availability (available, unavailable, or faulted) from separate inputs: an operator disable, a security disable, the firmware install state, the status the station reports for itself, and the connector statuses. The first matching rule wins:

1. Disabled by an operator or after a critical security event: unavailable.
2. Failed firmware install, a station-reported fault, or any faulted connector: faulted.
3. Firmware install in progress, or the station reports itself unavailable: unavailable.
4. Otherwise: available.

The station reports its own status on OCPP 1.6 connector 0, on OCPP 2.x EVSE 0, or through `NotifyEvent` with the `ChargingStation` component and the `AvailabilityState` variable. Connector 0 and EVSE 0 describe the station itself. They never appear as a connector or port.

A reboot (`BootNotification`) does not reset availability. A disable or a failed firmware install stays in place until it is cleared.

sections.heading: Enable and disable a station
sections.text:
Operators with the `stations:write` permission see an Enable Station or Disable Station button in the station detail header. Disable Station is a red button, because it stops new charging at the station.

1. Open the station detail page.
2. Click Disable Station. A confirmation dialog explains the effect.
3. Confirm. The CSMS marks the station unavailable and sends OCPP `ChangeAvailability` (Inoperative) to the station.

Drivers cannot start charging at a disabled station until you enable it. Sessions in progress are not stopped.

The header shows Enable Station when the station is disabled or its last firmware install failed. Enabling sends `ChangeAvailability` (Operative) and clears a failed firmware install.

To take a whole site out of service for a planned window, use a maintenance window instead.

sections.heading: Security auto-disable
sections.text: When a station reports a critical security event, the CSMS disables the station and sends OCPP `ChangeAvailability` (Inoperative), as it does for an operator disable. The `security.autoDisableOnCritical` setting controls this and is on by default. The History tab records the change with the triggering event. Click Enable Station to put the station back in service.

sections.heading: Effect on drivers
sections.text: When the whole station is unavailable (disabled, installing firmware, failed firmware install, or a station-reported fault), the driver portal shows "This station is unavailable right now. Try another station." and no connector can be selected. Portal and guest start requests return `409 STATION_UNAVAILABLE`. OCPI `START_SESSION` commands from roaming partners return `REJECTED`. A single faulted connector blocks only that connector.

sections.heading: API
sections.text: `PATCH /v1/stations/:id` accepts `availability` set to `available` or `unavailable`. The CSMS computes `faulted`, so the API rejects it with `400`. Station list and detail responses include `statusReason` and `reportedStatus`. Portal station and EVSE endpoints include `stationUnavailable`.

sections.heading: Security Profiles
sections.text:
| Profile | Authentication | Transport |
|---------|---------------|-----------|
| No Auth | None | ws:// (unencrypted) |
| Basic Auth | Basic Auth (password) | ws:// |
| TLS + Basic Auth | Basic Auth (password) | wss:// (TLS) |
| Mutual TLS | Client certificate | wss:// (mutual TLS) |

Mutual TLS stations do not require a password. The station presents a client certificate for authentication.

sections.heading: Station passwords
sections.text:
Basic Auth passwords are 16 to 40 characters for OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1 and 16 to 20 characters for OCPP 1.6. Allowed characters are letters, digits, and `* - _ = : + | @ .`. Rotate Credentials on the Security tab sets a new random 20-character password that works for every version.

When the station is online on Basic Auth or TLS + Basic Auth, the CSMS sends the new password to the station: `SetVariables(SecurityCtrlr.BasicAuthPassword)` for OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1, `ChangeConfiguration(AuthorizationKey)` with the hex-encoded password for OCPP 1.6. The CSMS saves the new password only after the station accepts it. If the station rejects it or does not answer, the old password stays valid. When the station is offline, the CSMS saves the password and you configure the station to match on site. A password command is never queued: if the station disconnects before the command reaches it, the change fails and the old password stays valid.

Change a station password only with Change Password or Rotate Credentials on the Security tab, or through the API with `POST /v1/stations/{id}/credentials`. Change the security profile on the same tab or with `PATCH /v1/stations/{id}`. The generic OCPP command routes refuse a password write with `400 STATION_CREDENTIALS_ROUTE_REQUIRED` (see Error Codes):

- `POST /v1/ocpp/commands/v21/SetVariables` with `SecurityCtrlr.BasicAuthPassword`
- `POST /v1/ocpp/commands/v16/ChangeConfiguration` with `AuthorizationKey`
- `POST /v1/ocpp/commands/v21/SetNetworkProfile` with `connectionData.basicAuthPassword`

Configuration templates cannot hold these variables either.

sections.heading: Station passwords
sections.text: The CSMS keeps station passwords out of its logs. The OCPP message log (requests and responses, in both directions) and the API access log show the password as `[redacted]`. A station configuration value that holds a password is stored as `[redacted]`. Passwords stored by earlier releases are replaced with `[redacted]` when the database is migrated.

sections.heading: Failed login throttling
sections.text: After 5 wrong passwords for one station within 60 seconds, the OCPP server refuses that station for 60 seconds. It answers HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header and does not check the password. A station with a wrong password therefore cannot slow down the connections of other stations. The connection log on the station Security tab records each refusal as `auth_failed` with the reason `Too many failed password attempts`. A station whose last successful login is still cached connects during the lockout. A successful login clears the count. Each OCPP server process keeps its own count.

sections.heading: Changing the security profile
sections.text:
For an offline station, the new profile is saved directly. Configure the station to match on site.

For an online station, the CSMS upgrades the station over OCPP:

- OCPP 2.1: the CSMS writes a new network connection profile with the higher profile (`SetNetworkProfile`), puts it first in `NetworkConfigurationPriority`, and resets the station when idle. Moving from `ws://` to TLS uses the CSMS TLS address in `OCPP_STATION_TLS_URL`. The station must already trust the CSMS server certificate, and for Mutual TLS it must hold a client certificate, or it rejects the change.
- OCPP 2.0.1: the CSMS asks for the Network Interface the station uses for the new profile: Wired 0 (the default) to Wired 3, or Wireless 0 to Wireless 3. It then writes a new network connection profile (`SetNetworkProfile`) with the address the station connects on now, or with `OCPP_STATION_TLS_URL` when moving from `ws://` to TLS, and with the station's message timeout (30 seconds when the station does not report one). From No Auth, the CSMS first sets the station password. It puts the new profile first in `NetworkConfigurationPriority` and resets the station when idle. The same certificate requirements as for OCPP 2.1 apply.
- OCPP 1.6: the CSMS sets `SecurityProfile` with `ChangeConfiguration` and resets the station.

The new profile shows as pending until the station reconnects with it. Until then the station can still connect with its current profile, so a failed upgrade does not lock it out. A station that cannot connect with the new settings falls back to its previous connection, and the upgrade stays pending. After the station connects with the new profile, the CSMS rejects the old one. Select the current profile to cancel a pending upgrade.

sections.heading: Changing the security profile
sections.text:
Through the API, an upgrade of a connected OCPP 2.0.1 station needs `ocppInterface` (`Wired0` to `Wired3`, `Wireless0` to `Wireless3`) in `PATCH /v1/stations/{id}` or `PATCH /v1/css/stations/{stationId}`. Without it the API answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. The CSMS records the address a station connects on at each connection. Until it has one, the upgrade answers `400 STATION_ENDPOINT_URL_UNKNOWN` (see Error Codes).

OCPP does not allow lowering the security profile of a connected station. Lower profiles are disabled while the station is online. To downgrade, take the station offline, change the profile, and reconfigure the station on site.

sections.heading: Connector Types
sections.text:
| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| CCS2 | Combined Charging System (common in North America and Europe) |
| CHAdeMO | DC fast charging (common in Japan) |
| Type2 | AC charging (European standard) |
| Type1 | AC charging (North American standard) |
| GBT | AC/DC charging (Chinese standard) |
| Tesla | Tesla proprietary connector |
| NACS | North American Charging Standard |

sections.heading: Station Detail
sections.text:
Click any station in the list to open the detail page. The detail page has the following tabs.

The header shows the online badge, the station status badge, and the Enable Station or Disable Station action. See Enable and disable a station.

Prev and Next in the header open the previous or next station of the list and keep the tab you have open. When that station does not have the tab, its first tab opens.

sections.heading: Details
sections.text:
Edit station metadata: name, vendor, model, site assignment, security profile, and password. The station's OCPP connection URL is displayed for configuration reference.

When you move a station to another site, an active maintenance window at the old site releases it (the station is told it is Operative again unless you disabled it, and the maintenance message is cleared from its screen), and an active window at the new site applies to it at once. Sessions keep the site where they happened, so the revenue, metrics and reports of each site keep their history.

The AI Insights row shows whether automatic AI insights watch the station: In Scope, or Suppressed with the end date, who suppressed them and why. Users with the `stations:write` permission click Suppress, enter a reason and an optional end date, and confirm. Until the end date, or until Resume, no new insight or suggested action is created for the station, its open insights are dismissed, and its waiting actions expire. An active maintenance event that covers the station suppresses them too. The stations list filters by AI Insights and marks suppressed stations with a badge.

A station also counts as suppressed while its site is suppressed (see Sites). The row then shows Suppressed with its site with a link to the site, and Resume is hidden until the site resumes. Suppress on the station still works: the station's own suppression stays in effect after the site resumes. Resuming a station while its site is suppressed is refused (`STATION_SITE_SUPPRESSED`).

sections.heading: Images
sections.text: Upload and manage station photos. Set a main image that displays in the station header. Tag images and mark them as driver-visible for display in the driver portal. Images are stored in S3 with presigned URLs for upload and download.

sections.heading: Metrics
sections.text: Station performance metrics including uptime percentage, utilization, total sessions, session success rate, energy delivered, average session duration, disconnect count, and average downtime, plus Total Revenue (incl. tax), Revenue (excl. tax), Tax Collected, electricity cost, and Profit. Revenue follows the dashboard definition.

sections.heading: Sessions
sections.text: Paginated list of all charging sessions for this station. Filterable by status and date range.

sections.heading: Connectors
sections.text:
View and manage EVSEs and connectors. Each connector shows its current status with a color-coded badge. Add new EVSEs and connectors, edit connector types and power ratings, or delete unused ones (blocked if in use).

Retire EVSE and Retire Connector take hardware out of service and keep its history. Drivers and roaming partners no longer see it, it takes no new sessions or reservations, the station status and uptime leave it out, and the station is told it is Inoperative. A retired EVSE or connector shows a Retired badge, and Restore EVSE or Restore Connector puts it back in service. Retire is refused while the hardware is in use or holds an active or upcoming reservation. Delete is only for hardware without history: retire an EVSE or connector that sessions, reservations or meter values refer to. A status report the station sends for a retired connector is stored, and the connector stays retired until you restore it.

EVSE numbers are unique per station, and connector numbers are unique per EVSE.

OCPP 1.6 stations

An OCPP 1.6 station has no EVSEs. The CSMS stores connector N as EVSE N with a single connector N.

- In the Create EVSE dialog, the connector number follows the EVSE number and cannot be edited.
- The Create Connector button is hidden, because a 1.6 EVSE holds exactly one connector.
- `POST /v1/stations/:id/evses` and `POST /v1/stations/:id/evses/:evseId/connectors` return `400 CONNECTOR_ID_MISMATCH` when the request breaks this rule.

Max power

sections.heading: Connectors
sections.text:
A connector the CSMS creates automatically, because the station reported a connector it did not know, starts without a max power. OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1 stations fill it in from their configuration report (`NotifyReport`, the `maxLimit` of the `EVSE` component's `Power` variable). The report never replaces a value an operator set. OCPP 1.6 has no equivalent report.

A connector without a max power shows a Max power unknown badge. Load management cannot cap the connector at its rating until you set it, so it caps the connector at its equal share of the circuit. Click Edit EVSE to set the max power.

| Status | Color | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| available | Green | Ready for use |
| charging | Blue | Actively charging |
| occupied | Blue | In use (OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1) |
| preparing | Cyan | Cable plugged in, not yet charging |
| ev_connected | Cyan | EV connected (OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1) |
| reserved | Orange | Reserved for a driver |
| suspended_ev | Yellow | Paused by vehicle |
| suspended_evse | Yellow | Paused by station |
| idle | Yellow | Transaction active, no energy demand |
| finishing | Violet | Session ending |
| discharging | Blue | V2G energy flow |
| faulted | Red | Hardware fault |
| unavailable | Red | Out of service |

sections.heading: Commands
sections.text:
Send OCPP commands to the station and view the real-time OCPP message log. Available commands include Reset, UnlockConnector, ChangeAvailability, TriggerMessage, GetBaseReport (2.0.1 and 2.1), GetConfiguration (1.6), and more.

The tab offers only the commands the station's OCPP version defines. For an OCPP 2.0.1 station it hides the commands that exist only in OCPP 2.1, and the command forms follow the OCPP 2.0.1 schema. A command with a value OCPP 2.0.1 cannot carry, such as a 2.1-only charging profile purpose or display message format, is refused with `400 OCPP_VERSION_MISMATCH` and nothing is sent to the station.

The OCPP Message Log shows all OCPP messages exchanged between the station and the CSMS, and the commands queued for it while it is offline. The Type column shows CALL, RESULT, or ERROR. The Status column shows Processed for a message exchanged with the station and Queued for a command that waits in the offline queue. Hover Queued to read "Sent when the station reconnects".

Destructive commands require confirmation. Reset, ChangeAvailability, and ClearCache each open a confirmation dialog before dispatching, since a misclick can wipe runtime state, disable a revenue-generating EVSE, or force every cached idToken to re-authorize.

Offline stations queue the command. When the target station is not connected to any OCPP pod, the API returns `202 Accepted` with code `COMMAND_QUEUED` and the UI shows a yellow Queued badge on the response card. The command is held in the offline queue and dispatched on the next reconnect. The command dialog then shows no Send button, so the same command cannot be queued twice from it.

sections.heading: Commands
sections.text: Every dispatch is audited. Each command dispatched through the OCPP Commands tab writes a row to the per-station audit log with `action: 'command_dispatched'`, the actor, the OCPP action name, the outcome (`accepted`, `queued (station offline)`, `timeout`, or `error: `), and a payload snapshot. Payloads are capped at 16 KB to keep audit rows lean. Oversized payloads are replaced with a `_truncated` marker referencing the original size. View the audit trail under the History tab on the station detail page or globally at `/audit`.

sections.heading: Simulate
sections.text: Available for simulator stations only. Trigger physical actions on the simulated station: plug in, authorize, start charging, stop charging, unplug, inject fault, and power cycle. See Simulator Actions for details.

sections.heading: Security
sections.text: Manage the station's authentication credentials. Change the security profile, set or rotate the Basic Auth password (Basic Auth and TLS + Basic Auth), and cancel a pending profile upgrade. View the security event log: connection attempts, password changes, profile changes and the security events the station reports. Filter it by source, event, severity and date range, and click a row to see its details as formatted JSON. For Mutual TLS stations, the password section is hidden and a note directs to the Certificates tab. See Security Profiles for how changes reach the station.

sections.heading: Connectivity
sections.text: The SIM status, cellular data sessions, SIM alerts and modem signal of a cellular station, a timeline of its connects and disconnects with the likely cause of each disconnect, and Reset Network. The tab, and the ICCID and IMSI field on the Details tab, show only while a SIM provider or station signal reads are on (off by default). See Station Connectivity.

sections.heading: Certificates
sections.text: Available for OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1 stations when Plug and Charge is enabled. View installed certificates, install new CA certificates, query the station for its certificate inventory, and delete certificates. See Certificates for details.

sections.heading: Display Messages
sections.text: Available for OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1 stations. Send display messages to the station screen via OCPP SetDisplayMessage. View active messages, clear them, and refresh the list from the station via GetDisplayMessages.

sections.heading: Meter Values
sections.text: View standalone meter value readings from the station outside of transaction context.

sections.heading: Events
sections.text: Available for OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1 stations. View the monitoring events the station reports through `NotifyEvent`, such as threshold breaches, periodic readings and component status changes. Click a row to see its event data as formatted JSON. Security events are in the security event log on the Security tab.

sections.heading: Configurations
sections.text: View the station's current OCPP configuration as a read-only table. Click Refresh from Station to pull the latest configuration from the station via GetConfiguration (1.6) or GetBaseReport (2.0.1 and 2.1). Push a configuration template to update station settings.

sections.heading: Firmware Updates
sections.text: View the firmware update operations for this station, including status (downloading, downloaded, installing, installed, failed) and timestamps. A station that is installing firmware is unavailable. A failed install marks the station faulted until the next install or until an operator enables the station.

sections.heading: Charging Profiles
sections.text: View and manage OCPP charging profiles on the station. Refresh profiles from the station, push new profiles from templates, clear existing ones, and view the composite schedule. See Smart Charging for template management.

sections.heading: QR Codes
sections.text:
Generate and download QR codes for each EVSE on the station. QR codes link to the driver portal charging flow at `/charge/:stationId/:evseId`.

Dynamic QR codes

A static QR code is printed once and never changes. A dynamic QR code is shown on the station's display and changes over time. Its URL holds a time-based one-time password (TOTP). The station makes a new password every validity period, and the portal checks the password when a driver scans the code. A photo or copy of the code stops working once its password expires.

Dynamic QR codes work only on OCPP 2.1 stations whose firmware implements the `WebPaymentsCtrlr` component and that have a display that can show a changing QR code. Other stations use the static QR code. OCPP 1.6 and 2.0.1 stations show a note instead of the settings.

The Dynamic QR codes card on the QR Codes tab shows the station support:

- Supported: the station reports `WebPaymentsCtrlr`.
- Not supported: the station does not know `WebPaymentsCtrlr`, lacks a setting the feature needs, or reports it as not available. Enable is disabled.
- Unknown: the station is offline, did not answer, or was not checked yet.

When the card opens, it uses the station's last device model report from the past 24 hours, if there is one. Select Check support to ask the online station now. The CSMS sends GetVariables for `WebPaymentsCtrlr` and shows the answer with the time of the check. Check support sends a command to the station, so it needs the `stations:write` permission.

To enable dynamic QR codes:

1. Make sure the station is online.
2. Enter Password validity (seconds), from 6 to 3600 (default 60). The station shows each code for this long.
3. Enter Password length, from 6 to 32 characters (default 8).
4. Select Enable.

sections.heading: QR Codes
sections.text:
The CSMS sends the station its `WebPaymentsCtrlr` settings: a URL template that points to the portal, the TOTP version, the validity, the length, and a new random shared secret. The card turns On only when the station accepts every setting. Each code then opens `/qr/:stationId/:evseId/:password/v1` on the portal.

You can select Enable before a support check. When the station answers that it does not know `WebPaymentsCtrlr`, or its last report shows the component as not available, the CSMS shows that the station does not support dynamic QR codes and stores nothing.

Update and rotate secret sends the entered validity and length with a new shared secret. Codes made with the old secret stop working. Use it to change the settings or when the secret may have leaked.

Disable asks for confirmation, then turns dynamic QR codes off on the station and removes the stored secret. The portal refuses every code the station showed before. When the station is offline, the CSMS removes the secret at once, so its codes are refused.

A station can let the driver enter a maximum cost, energy, or time before it shows the code. The station adds them to the code URL as `maxcost`, `maxenergy` (Wh), and `maxtime` (seconds), and the session uses them as limits, the same as with a static QR code.

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.text: View the active tariff resolved for this station, the pricing formula breakdown, and the full schedule of tariffs that apply at different times. Assign or remove a pricing group.

sections.heading: Local Auth List
sections.text: Manage the station's local authorization list. Add driver tokens, remove entries, and push the curated list to the station via OCPP SendLocalList. Changes are database-only until you explicitly push. See Tokens for token management.

sections.heading: Authorize Log
sections.text: Visible to operators with the `drivers:read` permission. Cross-token forensic view filtered to this station: every Authorize attempt (and OCPP 1.6 StartTransaction without prior Authorize) the station has produced, with the matched token, matched driver, outcome (accepted / blocked / expired / concurrent_tx / no_credit / db_error), OCPP version, and a reason tag. Useful for diagnosing why a card was rejected at a specific station.

sections.heading: Reservations
sections.text: Available when reservations are enabled in settings. View reservations for this station, create new ones, and cancel existing reservations.

sections.heading: AI Insights
sections.text: Lists the automatic insights about the station and its sessions, newest first, with their status. Click a row to open the insight. The tab shows to users with the `aiInsights:read` permission while AI Insights are on. The light bulb button above the assistant button opens this tab and pulses while an insight is open or its action waits for a decision.

sections.heading: History
sections.text: Per-station audit trail. Every operator-initiated change to the station (edits, command dispatches, approval changes) is recorded with the actor, the before/after state, and a timestamp.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Support cases provide a ticketing system for resolving driver issues. Operators create and manage cases from the CSMS. Drivers create cases from the portal. Each case has a threaded message history, file attachments, linked charging sessions, and the ability to issue per-session refunds.

sections.heading: Create a Support Case
sections.text:
1. Navigate to Support Cases in the sidebar.
2. Click Create Case.
3. Select a category and priority, and optionally a driver and an operator under Assigned To.
4. Enter a subject and description.
5. Optionally link one or more charging sessions.
6. Click Create.

The system generates a case number (e.g., CASE-00001) from a PostgreSQL sequence.

Drivers can also create cases from the portal. When a driver clicks Report Issue on a session detail page, the session is automatically linked to the new case.

sections.heading: Case Detail
sections.text: Click any case in the list to open the detail page.

sections.heading: Message Thread
sections.text:
The message thread shows all messages in chronological order. Operators can send two types of messages:

- Public messages - Visible to both the operator and the driver.
- Internal notes - Visible to operators only. Marked with a distinct visual style.

System messages are automatically generated when the case status, priority, or assignment changes.

sections.heading: Attachments
sections.text:
Attach files to any message. Click the paperclip icon when composing a message, select files, and send. Attachments need S3 storage (see Settings).

Allowed file types:

- Images (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF)
- PDF
- CSV, plain text, and log files
- JSON and JSONL

The maximum file size is the Maximum attachment size (bytes) limit in Settings > AI > Usage and Limits (10 MB by default). Drivers who attach files in the portal get the same checks.

The server checks every file before it stores it:

- It checks the file content against the declared type and refuses a mismatch.
- It re-encodes images and removes their metadata, such as camera and location data.
- It refuses encrypted PDFs and cuts text files to 2 MB.

Click an attachment to preview an image or download the file. A download always saves the file instead of opening it in the browser.

With a self-managed S3 bucket, add a CORS rule that allows `POST` from the CSMS origin. The browser uploads files straight to the bucket, and uploads fail without this rule.

sections.heading: Linked Sessions
sections.text: Link charging sessions to a case for context. The case detail shows linked sessions with their transaction IDs. Add or remove session links from the sidebar controls.

sections.heading: Sidebar Controls
sections.text:
The right sidebar provides controls for:

- Status - Update the case status.
- Priority - Change the priority level.
- Category - Reclassify the case.
- Assigned To - Assign the case to an operator.

sections.heading: Case Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| open | New case, not yet addressed |
| in_progress | Operator is working on the case |
| waiting_on_driver | Operator needs information from the driver |
| resolved | Issue has been resolved |
| closed | Case is closed |
| ai_assist | The driver AI handles the case (shown as With the AI). See Driver AI Support |

sections.heading: Case Categories
sections.text:
| Category | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| billing_dispute | Billing or payment disagreement |
| charging_failure | Session did not charge correctly |
| connector_damage | Physical damage to a connector |
| account_issue | Driver account problem |
| payment_problem | Payment processing failure |
| reservation_issue | Reservation-related problem |
| general_inquiry | General question or feedback |

sections.heading: Case Priority
sections.text:
| Priority | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| low | Non-urgent, handle when available |
| medium | Standard priority (default for driver-created cases) |
| high | Requires prompt attention |
| urgent | Requires immediate attention |

sections.heading: Per-Session Refunds
sections.text:
Issue a refund for any session linked to the case:

1. Click Refund next to a linked session in the case detail.
2. Enter a refund amount (leave blank for a full refund).
3. Confirm the refund.

Refunds can be issued on sessions with `captured` or `partially_refunded` payment status. Partial refunds are supported.

sections.heading: Unread Indicators
sections.text:
The support cases navigation item shows a green pulsing dot when there are unread cases assigned to you. A case is marked as read when you view the detail page. New driver messages reset the read status.

Unread cases appear with bold text in the list view.

Cases with the driver AI do not count as unread until they reach the support team.

sections.heading: Notifications
sections.text:
The system sends notifications for support case events:

- Driver notifications: Case created (by operator), operator reply, case resolved, automatic answer ready (driver AI support).
- Operator notifications: New case from driver, driver reply. A case the driver sent to the AI notifies operators only when it reaches the support team.

sections.heading: Driver AI Support
sections.text:
Driver AI support gives a driver an automatic first answer to a new case, but only when the driver allows it. It is off by default. Turn it on with Offer AI analysis to drivers in Settings > AI > Driver Support (see Settings), and choose a provider that has an API key.

Before you turn driver AI support on, have the consent notice text reviewed against your privacy obligations. The notice is built in and versioned. You cannot edit it.

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.text:
1. In the portal or the mobile app, the driver opening a case chooses Ask AI first or Send to the team. Nothing is preselected. The notice tells the driver that the request and their own data go to an external AI provider. See Support Cases in the portal guide.
2. With Send to the team, the case reaches your team at once, as any other case. Nothing is sent to the AI.
3. With Ask AI first, the case gets the status With the AI. The AI reads the case and the driver's own sessions, payments, reservations, tokens (last 4 characters) and the stations used, and writes one answer. It has no tools and changes nothing.
4. The driver answers Did this solve your issue?. Yes resolves the case. No sends it to your team.

The AI gives one answer per case and holds no conversation. The case reaches your team when:

- The driver answers No.
- The driver writes a message before answering.
- The driver gives no answer within Wait for the driver's feedback (hours).
- The AI cannot answer: a driver limit, a token budget, a provider error, or an answer that fails the safety checks.
- You change the status of the case yourself.

A driver who writes on a case the AI resolved opens it again, and it reaches your team. A case you resolved does not reopen this way.

sections.heading: Finding Cases With the AI
sections.text:
Cases with the AI are left out of the default case list, the unread count, the open case counts, and the operator notifications until they reach your team. To see them:

- Select With the AI in the Status filter.
- Select a state in the AI State filter: Queued, Analyzing, Waiting for Driver Feedback, Resolved by AI, Passed to Support, AI Analysis Failed, or AI Analysis Skipped.
- Select AI or Support team in the Resolved by filter to list resolved cases by who resolved them.

Cases the AI resolved stay in the default list with the status Resolved. A badge next to the status shows the AI state of a case, or Resolved by AI.

sections.heading: AI on the Case Detail
sections.text:
The Driver Consent card on the case detail shows:

- Decision: Allowed AI analysis, Declined AI analysis, or Not asked.
- Answered at: when the driver chose, in server time.
- Notice Language and Notice Version: the notice the driver read.
- AI State and its reason, for example The driver reached the daily limit or No feedback from the driver.
- Automatic Answer at and Driver Feedback at.
- Resolved by: AI or Support team.

The automatic answer appears in the message thread as Automatic Answer. The History section lists the AI steps: AI analysis allowed, AI analysis declined, Automatic answer given, Resolved by AI, Passed from AI to support, and AI Analysis Failed. The Status control shows With the AI but you cannot select it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text:
These limits send a case straight to your team when the driver or the company reaches them. Set them in Settings > AI > Driver Support, except the monthly budgets.

| Limit | Default | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| AI-analyzed requests per driver per day | 3 | Counted per day in the system timezone |
| AI requests per driver per minute | 2 | Checked when the driver creates the case |
| Tokens per driver per day | 40,000 | Midnight to midnight UTC. 0 means no limit |
| Wait for the driver's feedback (hours) | 24 | A case without feedback after this time goes to your team |
| Company tokens per month | 0 (no limit) | In Settings > AI > Usage and Limits |
| Tokens per site per month | 0 (no limit) | Counts the site of the case's station. In Settings > AI > Usage and Limits |

The tokens of driver AI support appear under Driver Support in the AI usage. See AI Usage and Budgets.

sections.heading: AI-Assisted Replies
sections.text: When support AI is turned on in Settings > AI > Support Drafts, users with the `support:write` permission see an AI Draft button in the message input area. Check Internal note for a note to your team, or leave it unchecked for a reply to the customer. The draft streams into the message box. Click Stop draft to end it early. A Sources list shows the data the AI read. The AI reads only the case and its linked data, follows the driver's language in customer replies, and never changes anything or sends a message. See AI Assistant for details.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Tokens are authentication credentials that identify drivers when they start a charging session. A driver can have multiple tokens. The CSMS validates tokens during the OCPP Authorize flow before allowing a session to begin.

sections.heading: Token Types
sections.text:
The token type is the OCPP 2.1 IdToken type. Every form offers the same list.

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| ISO14443 | UID of an RFID card or key fob. Most cards use this type. |
| ISO15693 | UID of an ISO 15693 RFID card. |
| KeyCode | A code the driver enters at the station, such as a PIN. |
| eMAID | Plug and Charge contract identifier (ISO 15118). |
| EVCCID | Identifier of the vehicle's charging controller (ISO 15118). |
| MacAddress | MAC address of the vehicle. |
| VIN | Vehicle identification number. |
| Central | An identifier the CSMS issues, for example for app starts. |
| Local | An identifier the station creates. |
| DirectPayment | A payment terminal reference. |
| NoAuthorization | A marker for charging without authorization. |

Drivers who add a card in the portal choose from ISO14443, ISO15693, KeyCode, eMAID, EVCCID, MacAddress, VIN and Local.

sections.heading: Create a Token
sections.text:
1. Navigate to Tokens in the sidebar.
2. Click Create Token.
3. Enter the Token Value. For an RFID card, this is the card UID.
4. Choose the Token Type.
5. Optionally select the Driver to assign the token to.
6. Click Create.

Drivers can also add RFID cards themselves through the portal's Account page.

sections.heading: Token Detail
sections.text:
Click any token in the list to view its detail page.

The detail page has four tabs:

- Token Details - token value, type, assigned driver, creation date, and active status. Edit and Delete actions live here.
- Sessions - charging sessions whose OCPP Authorize matched this specific token (filtered by `charging_sessions.token_id`, not driver id).
- History - paginated `token_audit_log` showing every lifecycle event (created, updated, activated, deactivated, revoked, deleted, imported) with the actor name (operator or driver, linked to their detail page) and free-text notes.
- Authorize Log - paginated `authorize_attempts` filtered to this token, including the matched outcome (accepted / blocked / expired / concurrent_tx / no_credit / db_error). Useful for forensic triage when a driver reports a swipe was rejected.

sections.heading: Token Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Active | Token can be used to authenticate and start sessions |
| Revoked | Token was deactivated and is rejected as Blocked |
| Inactive | Token is turned off without a recorded deactivation time and is rejected as Blocked |
| Expired | Token is active but past its expiry and is rejected as Expired |

Toggle a token between active and inactive from the detail page. Deactivated tokens are rejected by the OCPP authorize handler. For a deactivated token, the Details tab shows when it was deactivated, by whom (Operator, Driver or System), and the reason.

sections.heading: Expiry
sections.text: Set Expires on the token's edit form, or leave it empty for a token that does not expire. After that time stations refuse the token as Expired. A token on a local authorization list carries its expiry to the station.

sections.heading: Reactivation by Drivers
sections.text: A driver can turn a card back on in the portal only when the driver turned it off. A card the operator deactivated stays off until an operator reactivates it. The portal shows it as deactivated by the operator.

sections.heading: Deactivated Drivers
sections.text: When a driver is deactivated, the driver's tokens are deactivated. While the driver is inactive, you cannot create a token for the driver, reactivate one of the driver's tokens, or assign an active token to the driver. The CSMS also refuses an active token of an inactive driver at authorization.

sections.heading: Delete a Token
sections.text:
Operator delete from the dashboard is a hard delete - the `driver_tokens` row is removed. To preserve historical session linkage and the audit trail, the system blocks deletion when an active charging session still references the token: `DELETE /v1/tokens/:id` returns `409 TOKEN_IN_USE` until the session ends. Cancel or finish the session, then retry.

Driver-side removal from the portal is a soft delete - the row stays with `is_active = false` and `revoked_reason = "Removed by driver"`. The token can be re-added later by the same driver without losing its historical link to past sessions.

sections.heading: Authorization Flow
sections.text:
When a driver taps an RFID card or authenticates through the app:

1. The station sends an OCPP Authorize request with the token value.
2. The CSMS looks up the token in the `driver_tokens` table.
3. If found, active and not expired, and its driver is active, the CSMS checks for an existing active session referencing the same token. If one exists at any station, the response is `ConcurrentTx` and the attempt is recorded with outcome `concurrent_tx`. This prevents a single card from starting two sessions simultaneously.
4. If found, active, and not concurrent, the CSMS returns Accepted.
5. If not found locally, the CSMS checks OCPI external tokens from roaming partners.
6. If the station's site has free vend enabled, any token is accepted regardless of lookup result.

On OCPP 2.1, a token of type Local is accepted without a lookup, since the station created it. A token of type Central that the CSMS does not know is refused as Invalid, unless it is the id the CSMS sent that station to start a charge or hold a reservation: a station should never ask to authorize a Central token.

Stations using a cached local authorization list may skip the Authorize message and go straight to StartTransaction (OCPP 1.6) or TransactionEvent (OCPP 2.1). The CSMS validates the token in those handlers too and writes the same `authorize_attempts` rows, so the forensic log captures the decision regardless of which path the station takes.

sections.heading: Authorize Log
sections.text:
Every Authorize attempt - and every OCPP 1.6 StartTransaction or OCPP 2.1 TransactionEvent (Started) that arrives without a prior Authorize - is recorded in `authorize_attempts` with the matched token, matched driver, outcome, OCPP version, and a short reason tag. Stations using a local authorization list skip the explicit Authorize call, so the StartTransaction / TransactionEvent path is the only forensic record for those flows.
