Do not use the React Native `Modal` component on this build. On the New Architecture (Fabric and Bridgeless) it renders blank and freezes the screen. Render overlays in-tree instead: confirm dialogs as a root absolute view, and sheets through the in-app `Portal` host. See the app's `docs/modal-freeze-newarch.md`.

sections.heading: Adding a screen
sections.text:
1. Create a file under `app/`. The path becomes the route. For example, `app/(tabs)/account/about.tsx` is `/account/about`.
2. Render with the shared `Screen` and design-system components so the screen inherits the backdrop, safe areas, and theming.
3. Fetch data with a hook in `src/features/` rather than calling the API inline.
4. Add any new strings to the locale files.

sections.heading: Verifying a change
sections.text:
Most edits hot-reload through Metro. Some changes need a full relaunch:

- i18n and native config changes (terminate and relaunch the app, not just a Metro reload).
- Brand or `app.config.ts` changes (restart Metro or rebuild).

Run a typecheck and lint before you consider a change done. See Testing.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Account tab is the hub for everything about you: your profile, security, payment methods, RFID cards, vehicles, favorites, support, and app information. It shows your name, email, and the date you joined.

sections.heading: Personal info
sections.text:
Tap Personal Info to edit your first and last name and your phone number. Your email is shown but cannot be changed here. When your account uses two-factor authentication, the app tells you to change the phone number in the driver portal, where you confirm the change. Below that, set your preferences:

- Language - the app updates immediately when you change it.
- Distance unit - miles or kilometers.
- Timezone - used for session and statement times.
- Show prices - Including tax (gross), Excluding tax (net), or the operator default. It sets whether charger prices and session costs are shown with or without tax. You pay the same amount either way. The choice is saved on your account, so the driver portal uses it too.

Save to apply your changes.

sections.heading: Invoices and billing address
sections.text: Tap Invoices to see your invoices and credit notes and share their PDFs. When your fleet invoices you for your sessions, add your billing address so it prints on your invoices. See Payments.

sections.heading: Security
sections.text:
Tap Security to protect your account. Here you can:

- Change your password.
- Set up two-factor authentication, using an authenticator app or email. Turning it off needs a code of your second factor or a recovery code, which the app cannot send, so the app tells you to turn it off in the driver portal.
- Turn on Require Face ID / fingerprint so the app opens only with biometrics.

sections.heading: Notifications
sections.text: Tap Notifications to choose how the operator reaches you. Toggle email, SMS, and push notifications on or off. These control delivery; the bell in the header always keeps an in-app copy. See Support for the notification inbox.

sections.heading: About
sections.text: Tap About for the app and CSMS version numbers, the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy links, and your operator contact details: address, email, and phone.

sections.heading: Sign out
sections.text: Tap Sign Out at the bottom of the Account hub to sign out of the app. You will need your email and password, plus any MFA code, to sign back in.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Activity tab is your charging history. It shows every session by month, a trend chart of your cost, energy, or distance, and the CO₂ you avoided. From here you also open a monthly statement you can keep for your records.

sections.heading: Browse your sessions
sections.text:
1. Tap the Activity tab.
2. Use the arrows next to the month to move between months.
3. Scroll the Sessions list to see each session for that month.
4. Tap a session to open its full detail.

Each row shows the station, the date, the energy delivered, and the cost, followed by "incl. tax" when the session has tax.

A session billed to your fleet also shows the fleet and its billing state: Not invoiced yet, Invoiced to the fleet, or Paid by the fleet.

sections.heading: Read your trends
sections.text:
Above the list is a chart for the trailing six months. Use the toggle to switch what it measures:

- Cost - what you spent.
- Energy - kilowatt-hours delivered.
- Distance - estimated range added, based on your vehicles.

The selected month is highlighted. Tap any bar to jump to that month. Below the chart, a line shows the CO₂ you avoided for the month.

sections.heading: Open a monthly statement
sections.text:
1. On the Activity tab, tap Monthly statement.
2. Review the itemized list: each session with its date, location, energy, cost, and CO₂. The cost reads Cost (incl. tax) when a session cost includes tax.
3. The totals card at the top sums the session count, energy, cost, and CO₂ for the month.

Use the statement for expense reports or to reconcile your charging spend.

Assign a vehicle to your sessions so the Distance trend and the range estimates are accurate. You manage vehicles under Vehicles.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Favorites are the stations you charge at often. Save one and it is a tap away from the header on any main screen. You manage them under Account > Favorites, or with the star on a station.

sections.heading: Save a favorite
sections.text:
1. Open a station from search, nearby, or a QR scan.
2. Tap the star, or Add to Favorites, on the station detail.

The star at the top of the home and charge screens highlights in orange once you have at least one favorite.

sections.heading: Open your favorites
sections.text: Tap the star icon in the header, or open the Account tab and tap Favorites. Each entry shows the station name, address, whether it is online, and how many connectors are available. Tap one to go straight to its detail and start charging.

sections.heading: Remove a favorite
sections.text: On the Favorites list, tap the trash icon next to a station and confirm. You can also tap Remove from Favorites on the station detail.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Charge tab is where you find a place to charge. You can search by name or address, see chargers near your location, or scan the QR code printed on a charger. Each result leads to the station detail, where you pick a connector and start.

sections.heading: Search for a station
sections.text:
1. Tap the Charge tab.
2. Type a station name or address in the search box.
3. Tap a result to open the station detail.

Each result shows the station name, its site, how many connectors are available, and a status badge.

sections.heading: See chargers near you
sections.text: Under the search box is a Nearby section. The first time you use it, the app asks for permission to use your location. Allow it, and nearby stations appear automatically, closest first. If you do not grant location access, the Nearby list stays empty and you can still search by name.

sections.heading: Scan a QR code
sections.text:
1. On the Charge tab, tap Scan QR.
2. Allow camera access the first time.
3. Point the camera at the QR code on the charger.

The app reads the code, opens that station, and preselects the connector printed on the label, so you can start charging in one more tap.

Scanning is the fastest way to start at a station you are standing next to. The code points straight to the right connector, so you do not have to match port numbers by hand.

sections.heading: What you see at a station
sections.text: Opening a result takes you to the station detail: the address, the price, your default payment card, and a tile for each connector with its type, power, and live status. Prices are shown with or without tax as your Show prices choice in Account and settings sets, with a note such as "Prices include 19% tax". From there you select an available connector and start. See Start and stop a charge.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Before you can charge, you need an account with your charging operator. You can create one in the app, then sign in. This page covers sign-up, sign-in, password recovery, multi-factor authentication, and unlocking the app with Face ID or a fingerprint.

sections.heading: Create an account
sections.text:
1. Open the app and tap Create One on the sign-in screen.
2. Enter your first name, last name, email, and a password.
3. Tap Create Account.
4. Check your inbox for a verification email and confirm your address.

Some operators create your account for you (for example, a fleet or workplace). In that case you receive an invite or a temporary password and only need to sign in.

sections.heading: Sign in
sections.text:
1. Enter the email and password for your account.
2. Tap Sign In.
3. If your account uses multi-factor authentication, enter the one-time code on the next screen.

If your details are wrong, the app shows an error and you can try again. Tap the eye icon in the password field to check what you typed.

sections.heading: Recover your password
sections.text:
1. On the sign-in screen, tap Forgot Password?.
2. Enter your email and submit.
3. Open the reset link in the email and set a new password.
4. Return to the app and sign in with the new password.

sections.heading: Multi-factor authentication
sections.text: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds a second step at sign-in. You set it up in Account > Security, where you can choose an authenticator app (TOTP), email, or SMS. After it is on, every sign-in asks for a one-time code in addition to your password. See Account and settings.

sections.heading: Unlock with Face ID or fingerprint
sections.text: If your device supports it, you can lock the app behind your face or fingerprint so it stays private even when your phone is unlocked. Turn this on in Account > Security. After that, the app asks for biometric confirmation each time you open it.

sections.heading: End User Guide
sections.text: This guide is for drivers. It walks through every part of the EVtivity mobile app, from creating an account to charging, paying, reserving a connector, and getting support. Each page covers one area of the app with the screens you will actually see.

sections.heading: What the app does
sections.text:
The app is your charging account in your pocket. With it you can:

- Find a charger by search, by nearby location, or by scanning a QR code on the station.
- Start and stop a charging session and watch it live.
- Pay with a saved card.
- Reserve a connector for later.
- Review past sessions, monthly statements, and the CO₂ you avoided.
- Manage vehicles, RFID cards, favorite stations, and notifications.
- Open a support case and chat with the operator.

sections.heading: Getting the app
sections.text: Download the app from the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android). The exact name and icon depend on your charging network, because each operator publishes the app under its own brand. Open it and sign in, or create an account if you are new. See Getting started.

sections.heading: Finding your way around
sections.text:
The home screen greets you by name and shows your active session, your recent sessions, and quick links to Payment Methods, RFID Cards, Vehicles, and Support. The star and bell at the top open your favorite stations and your notifications.

The bottom of every screen has five tabs:

1. Home - your dashboard and quick actions.
2. Charge - find a charger and start a session.
3. Activity - your charging history and statements.
4. Reserve - book a connector for later.
5. Account - your profile, payment methods, and settings.

Some features depend on how your operator has set up their network. Reservations, roaming, and payments can be turned on or off, so a screen described here may not appear if your operator has disabled it.

sections.heading: The guides
sections.text:
- Getting started - create an account, sign in, and secure the app.
- Find a charger - search, nearby, and QR scan.
- Start and stop a charge - connectors, starting, the live screen, and stopping.
- Payments - add and manage saved cards.
- Reservations - book and cancel a connector.
- Activity and statements - history, trends, and invoices.
- Vehicles - add a car and estimate range.
- RFID cards - add and manage tap-to-charge cards.
- Favorites - save the stations you use most.
- Support - notifications and support chat.
- Account and settings - profile, security, and preferences.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
Charging is paid through a card you save in the app. Cards are stored by your operator's payment provider (Stripe or Adyen), so your full card number is never stored by the app or the operator. You manage cards under Account > Payment Methods.

Each saved card shows the brand, the last four digits, and a Default badge on the one in use.

sections.heading: Add a card
sections.text:
1. Open the Account tab and tap Payment Methods.
2. Tap Add a Card.
3. Enter your card number, expiry, and security code in the provider's secure card form.
4. Save. The app shows "Card saved" and the card appears in your list.

sections.heading: Card verification (3D Secure)
sections.text:
Your bank can ask you to confirm the card:

- Stripe: the verification opens inside the card sheet.
- Adyen: the app opens your bank's page. Confirm the card there, and you return to the app, which finishes saving the card.

If the bank refuses the card or the verification fails, the card is not saved and the app shows the reason.

sections.heading: Test mode
sections.text: When the operator runs the test payment provider, the app shows a Test mode badge ("No real card is charged. The test card you pick decides the outcome.") and a Choose a test card list instead of the card form. A card that requires authentication asks you to Confirm the card with Approve or Fail authentication.

sections.heading: Older app versions
sections.text:
If your app version does not support the operator's payment provider, the screen shows a message instead of the card form:

- "Update the app to add a card with this payment provider."
- "This app build cannot add a card with this payment provider. Install the latest version of the app."

Install the latest version from your app store. Cards you saved earlier keep working for charging in every version.

sections.heading: Set a default card
sections.text: The default card is the one used when you start a session. To change it, tap Set default on another card. The Default badge moves to it.

sections.heading: Remove a card
sections.text: Tap Remove on a card to delete it. If you remove your only card, add another before you start your next session.

sections.heading: Pay through your fleet
sections.text:
If your fleet bills your charging on account, the Payment Methods screen shows a note above your cards: "Your charging is billed to (your fleet). You need no payment method to charge." Your fleet pays these sessions, so you can charge without a saved card.

When you start a session, the station shows Billed to and your fleet in place of a card, with "Your fleet pays for this session. You need no payment method." See Start and stop a charge.

Each session billed to your fleet shows its billing state in Activity: Not invoiced yet, Invoiced to the fleet, or Paid by the fleet.

If you are opted out of your fleet's account billing, the note does not show and you pay with a card like any other driver.

sections.heading: Invoiced to you by your fleet
sections.text:
Some fleets invoice each member for their own sessions instead of paying the sessions themselves. You still charge without a card. The note on the Payment Methods screen then reads "Your charging is invoiced to you monthly via (your fleet). You need no payment method to charge." The station shows "Billed to you via" and your fleet, and your sessions show the state Not invoiced yet, Invoiced to you, or Paid.

Once a month you receive your invoice by email with the PDF attached and as a push notification. Tap the notification to open the invoice. A credit note or a reminder for an overdue invoice arrives the same way. These messages are always sent, whatever your notification settings.

sections.heading: Invoices
sections.text: Open the Account tab and tap Invoices to see your invoices and credit notes. Your monthly member invoices show the fleet they come through. Invoices the operator issued to you directly show too. Tap an invoice to see its period, dates, bill-to block, items and total. Tap Download PDF to open the PDF in the share sheet, where you can save or send it. See Invoices for what each field means.

sections.heading: Billing address
sections.text:
Your member invoices print your billing address. Add it on the billing address screen in the Account tab: Name on Invoice, Street, City, State or Region, Postal Code and Country. Leave Name on Invoice empty to use your first and last name. When your fleet invoices you and the address is empty, the app asks you to add it. Without an address, your invoices show your name and email. The driver portal shows and edits the same address.

Older versions of the app show only "Billed to" and your fleet for these sessions and have no invoices list. You still receive each invoice by email.

If your operator runs a free network, the Payment Methods screen may show that no card is required. When the operator has not set up payments, the screen shows "Payments are not set up for this operator."

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A reservation holds a connector so it is free when you arrive. The Reserve tab lists your upcoming and past reservations and lets you book a new one. Reservations are available only if your operator has turned them on.

sections.heading: Make a reservation
sections.text:
1. Tap the Reserve tab, then New Reservation.
2. Search for a station by name or address and select it.
3. Choose Now to start right away, or Schedule to pick a date and time within the next seven days.
4. Choose a duration: 30, 60, or 120 minutes.
5. Tap Confirm.

The reservation appears under Upcoming.

A reservation that starts now is sent to the station, and the app waits for the station to confirm the hold. If the station refuses or does not answer, the app shows an error and the reservation is cancelled with no fee. A scheduled reservation is sent to the station at its start time.

sections.heading: View your reservations
sections.text:
The Reserve tab has two tabs of its own:

- Upcoming - reservations that are scheduled or active now.
- Past - reservations that expired, were cancelled, or became a session.

Tap any reservation to see its full detail: the station, the start and expiry times, the connector, and its status. Pull down to refresh the list.

sections.heading: Start charging from a reservation
sections.text:
When your reservation is active, go to the station and start as usual, from the app or with the RFID card you last used. The connector is already held for you. If the reservation converts into a charging session, its detail links to that session.

Another driver cannot use your reservation. If someone else starts on the connector, you get a notification and no no-show fee applies.

If the station goes offline or reports a fault during your reservation, the reservation is cancelled, no fee is charged, and you get a notification.

sections.heading: Cancel a reservation
sections.text:
1. Open the reservation from the Upcoming list, or swipe it.
2. Tap Cancel Reservation.
3. Confirm with Cancel Reservation.

Some operators charge a fee if you cancel close to the start time or let a reservation expire unused. If a cancellation fee applies, the app warns you before you confirm. A no-show fee applies only when the station confirmed the hold and stayed available, and you did not charge. It is charged once.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
An RFID card lets you start a charge by tapping the card on the station reader, without opening the app. You manage your cards under Account > RFID Cards.

Each card is listed with its identifier masked except the last few characters, its standard (for example ISO14443), and an active toggle.

sections.heading: Add a card
sections.text:
1. Open the Account tab and tap RFID Cards.
2. Tap Add RFID Card.
3. Enter the card identifier printed on the card.
4. Tap Add. The card appears in your list, ready to use.

sections.heading: Activate or deactivate a card
sections.text:
Each card has a toggle:

- Activate turns the card on so it can start sessions.
- Deactivate turns it off, for example if you misplace it.

When you deactivate a card, the app asks you to confirm. The toggle then settles on the new state. You can reactivate the card later if you find it.

Deactivate a lost card right away. A deactivated card cannot start a session, so no one else can charge on your account with it.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Once you have opened a station, you choose a connector and start charging. While the session runs, the app shows live power, energy, and cost. You stop from the same screen when you are finished.

sections.heading: Start a session
sections.text:
1. Open the station from search, nearby, or a QR scan.
2. Check that a payment card is shown. Tap Change to pick a different one if needed.
3. Plug the cable into your vehicle.
4. Select an Available connector tile. Unavailable connectors are greyed out and cannot be selected.
5. Tap Start Charging.

The app checks that the cable is detected. If it is not, a message asks you to plug in and try again. When the station accepts the start, the app opens the live session screen.

You need a saved payment method before you can start, unless your operator runs a free network. Add one under Payments.

If your fleet bills your sessions on account, the station shows Billed to and your fleet in place of the card. You start without a card and your fleet pays the session.

sections.heading: When you already have a session
sections.text:
You can run only one charging session at a time. If a session is already in progress, opening any station replaces the connector list and Start Charging button with a notice.

Tap View Active Session to jump to the running session, where you can monitor or stop it. Once that session ends, the station detail shows the connectors and the Start Charging button again.

sections.heading: Watch a session live
sections.text:
The session screen updates while you charge. It shows:

- Current power in kilowatts and energy delivered in kilowatt-hours.
- Time elapsed and the running cost.
- Your vehicle battery estimate and the CO₂ you have avoided.
- Charts of power and energy over time.

The connector status animates while the session is active. You can assign a vehicle to the session to improve the range estimate, or open a support case if something looks wrong.

The live charts and the Stop Charging button appear only while a session is charging. After a session ends, the same screen shows the final totals and the receipt.

sections.heading: Stop a session
sections.text:
1. Open the active session from the home screen or the Activity tab.
2. Tap Stop Charging.
3. Confirm with Stop Charging in the dialog.

The station ends the session and the screen switches to the final summary: total energy, duration, cost, and CO₂ avoided.

sections.heading: After charging
sections.text:
A completed session stays in your history. Open it any time from Activity to see the breakdown, the site and address, the vehicle used, and the payment status. Costs include tax. With Show prices set to excluding tax, the breakdown shows the net amount, the tax, and the total. Set to including tax, it shows the total and the tax it contains. If you left the car plugged in after charging finished, an idle warning reminds you to unplug so others can use the connector.

For a session billed to your fleet, the detail shows Fleet billing with the fleet and the state: Not invoiced yet, Invoiced to the fleet, or Paid by the fleet. The fleet invoice goes to the fleet, not to you.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Station Watch tells you when a station frees up. When every connector is in use, or the station is offline, tap Notify me when free on its detail screen. The moment a connector becomes available, you get a notification through your usual channels (push, email, or SMS). It is one tap, and it clears itself once it fires.

sections.heading: Watch a station
sections.text:
1. Open a station from search, nearby, or a QR scan.
2. If no connector is free, a Notify me when free button appears below the favorites button.
3. Tap it. The button changes to Remove from Watching to confirm. Tap it again to stop watching.

The Notify me when free button only shows when the station has nothing available right now. If a connector is already free, there is nothing to wait for, so the button is hidden and you can start charging.

sections.heading: Get notified
sections.text:
When a connector at a watched station becomes available, EVtivity sends you a notification. It follows the same preferences as every other alert, which you set under Account > Notifications. Tap the notification to jump straight to the station and start charging.

A watch is one-shot: it clears itself as soon as it notifies you. If you miss the window and the station fills up again, open it and tap Notify me when free to re-arm.

sections.heading: Open your watches
sections.text: Tap the eye icon in the header, to the right of the favorites star. The icon shows a count badge when you have active watches. It opens the Watching list, where each entry shows the station name, address, and current availability. Tap the trash icon to stop watching a station.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- A watch expires on its own after 24 hours if the station never frees up.
- You can watch up to 25 stations at once.
- Starting a charge at a station you are watching clears that watch automatically.
- Watches are tied to your driver account and are separate from favorites.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: When you need help, the app lets you open a support case and chat with the operator in real time. The bell in the header keeps you up to date on sessions, reservations, and replies to your cases.

sections.heading: Notifications
sections.text: Tap the bell at the top of the home, charge, or account screen to open your notifications. They cover session receipts, when a charge starts and completes, reservation changes, and replies on your support cases. Opening the inbox marks the notifications as read and clears the badge. You choose which channels you receive (push, email, SMS) under Account and settings.

sections.heading: Open a support case
sections.text:
1. Open the Account tab and tap Support, or tap the Support card on the home screen.
2. Tap New Case.
3. If the screen asks How should we handle your request?, choose first (see Ask AI first).
4. Enter a subject, choose a category, and describe the problem.
5. Tap Submit. The case opens to its chat thread.

You can also reach support from a charging session, which links the case to that session so the operator has the details.

sections.heading: Ask AI first
sections.text:
When the operator offers it, a new case starts with a choice: let an AI analyze your issue first, or send the case straight to the support team. You choose for each case. The option shows only when the operator turned it on.

1. Tap New Case. The screen asks How should we handle your request? and shows About the AI analysis:
   - An AI gives an automatic first answer. It is not a promise, for example of a refund.
   - Your request and the data listed below are sent to an external AI provider.
   - You can still reach a person: answer No or write a message, and the support team takes over.
   - You decide for each request. If you send it to the support team, nothing is sent to the AI.
2. Open What the AI reads to see the data the AI uses: this request, your last 10 charging sessions of the past 30 days, your charging cards and tokens (last 4 characters only), your payments and reservations of the past 30 days, and the stations you used.
3. Tap Ask AI first or Send to the team. The two buttons are equal and nothing is selected for you. The form opens only after you choose.
4. Fill in the case and tap Submit.

The form shows your choice at the top. Tap Change to choose again before you submit. The notice also links to the operator's Privacy policy.

What the AI receives

The AI reads your request and your own charging sessions, payments, reservations and the stations you used. Stored credentials, such as passwords, are never sent. Card numbers and IBANs are cut to their last 4 characters. Email addresses and phone numbers are masked. Charging card and token ids are shortened to their last 4 characters.

With Send to the team, the case goes to the support team at once and nothing is sent to the AI.

sections.heading: The automatic answer
sections.text:
With Ask AI first, the case shows Analyzing your issue while the AI works. The app checks the case every few seconds while it is open, so the answer appears without a refresh. You also get a notification through the channels you chose.

The answer appears in the chat as Automatic answer, sometimes with suggested steps such as Try another connector. The AI gives one answer per case. It does not hold a conversation. Below the answer, the case asks Did this solve your issue?:

- Yes: the case is resolved and shows Resolved. You can reopen it by writing to us.
- No: the case goes to the support team and shows Sent to the support team.

The support team also takes over when you write a message before you answer, when you do not answer within the time the operator set (24 hours by default), or when the AI cannot answer, for example because of a provider error or a usage limit. The case then shows We sent your request to the support team. A case the AI resolved opens again and goes to the support team when you write a message on it.

sections.heading: Chat on a case
sections.text:
A case is a chat thread. Your messages appear on the right, the operator replies on the left, and grey system messages mark status changes. Type in the box at the bottom and send. You keep replying until the case is resolved.

The case header shows the case number, the category, and a status badge so you always know where it stands. Open any case again from the Support list, where cases are sorted with the most recently updated on top.

Open a case from the charging session that had the problem. The operator sees the station, connector, and time without you having to describe them.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Adding your vehicles lets the app estimate the range each session adds and feed the Distance trend on the Activity tab. You manage vehicles under Account > Vehicles.

sections.heading: Add a vehicle
sections.text:
1. Open the Account tab and tap Vehicles.
2. Tap Add Vehicle.
3. Choose the make, then the model, from the lists.
4. Optionally enter the year.
5. Tap Add.

The vehicle appears in your list with its make, model, and year.

sections.heading: Remove a vehicle
sections.text: Tap the trash icon next to a vehicle and confirm. Removing a vehicle does not change past sessions it was already assigned to.

sections.heading: Assign a vehicle to a session
sections.text:
When you open a charging session, you can assign one of your vehicles to it. The session then uses that vehicle efficiency to estimate the range added and the distance figures in your trends and statements. You can change the assigned vehicle on the session detail at any time.

If you drive more than one EV, add them all. Assign the right one to each session so your range and distance numbers stay accurate.

sections.heading: Mobile App
sections.text:
The EVtivity mobile app is an open-source driver application built with Expo and React Native. It runs on iOS and Android and talks to the same EVtivity CSMS backend that powers the web driver portal: drivers find chargers, start and stop sessions, manage payment methods and vehicles, view activity, make reservations, and open support cases.

This section has two parts. The End User Guide is for drivers and walks through using the app: finding chargers, starting sessions, paying, reserving, and getting support. The developer guides that follow cover running the app, changing it, building it, testing it on real devices, and shipping it to the app stores, plus white-labeling so a network operator can publish the app under its own brand.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.text:
- Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86 on the New Architecture (Fabric and Bridgeless).
- File-based routing with `expo-router`.
- Styling with NativeWind (Tailwind classes in React Native).
- Server state with TanStack Query, talking to the CSMS REST API.
- Local native modules for device attestation (Apple App Attest, Google Play Integrity).
- Six languages built in (English, Spanish, Simplified Chinese, German, Korean, Traditional Chinese), driver-selectable in-app.
- A white-label brand system so a single codebase ships under many brands.

The app is a thin client. All business logic, pricing, payments, and OCPP communication live in the CSMS. The app reads and writes through the `/v1/portal/*` API and reflects real-time changes through polling and server events.

sections.heading: How it connects to the CSMS
sections.text:
The API base URL is baked into the JavaScript bundle at build time from the `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` environment variable (falling back to the active brand's `apiUrl`). Every request carries the driver's bearer token. Sensitive flows are protected by device attestation, which the CSMS verifies server-side.

The app is the driver-facing counterpart to the web portal. If a feature exists in the portal, it almost always exists in the app and uses the same backend endpoint.

sections.heading: Languages
sections.text: The app ships full translations for six languages: English, Spanish, Simplified Chinese (简体中文), German (Deutsch), Korean (한국어), and Traditional Chinese (繁體中文). A driver picks their language in Account, and the choice applies immediately, persists across launches, and syncs to their server profile so emails and SMS use the same language. A white-label brand can narrow the offered set to any subset of the six; see White-labeling.

sections.heading: The guides
sections.text:
- Setup and first run - prerequisites, install, environment, and running the dev client.
- Configure Expo - `app.config.ts`, brands, environment variables, identifiers, and plugins.
- Making changes - project structure, conventions, and how to add a screen.
- Testing - typecheck, lint, and on-device verification.
- Run on a real device - Android over USB, iOS Simulator, and a physical iPhone.
- Build - development, preview, and production builds with EAS or locally.
- Push notifications - wiring APNs and FCM so push actually delivers.
- Submit to the app stores - App Store Connect and Google Play.
- White-labeling - run a network under your own brand.

sections.heading: Repository
sections.text: The app lives in its own open-source repository at github.com/EVtivity/evtivity-mobile-app. It is licensed under the same terms as the rest of the EVtivity platform. Clone it, point it at a CSMS instance, and you have a working driver app in minutes.

sections.heading: Push Notifications
sections.text: The app code for push is already in place. Live delivery needs three things tied to your accounts: an EAS project id, an Apple APNs key, and a Firebase (FCM) project. Until all three exist, the Push toggle in Account then Notifications saves a preference but no native push is delivered.

sections.heading: How push works
sections.text:
1. On launch the app requests permission, gets an Expo push token, and registers it with the CSMS at `/v1/portal/notifications/push-token`.
2. When a driver event fires (session, payment, reservation, support reply, automatic support answer), the CSMS sends a native push through Expo Push, which relays to APNs on iOS and FCM on Android.
3. Delivery only happens when the driver's `push_enabled` preference is true. The Push toggle sets that flag.
4. The in-app notification drawer is separate and always works, regardless of this setup.

sections.heading: Step 1: EAS project id
sections.text:
```bash
npx eas-cli login
npx eas-cli init
```

`eas init` prints a `projectId`. Because the config is dynamic, copy it into the active brand's `easProjectId` in `brands/`. Without it, no push token is minted. Simulators cannot get a device token, so test on a physical device.

sections.heading: Step 2: iOS (APNs)
sections.text:
```bash
npx eas-cli credentials
```

Choose iOS, then set up a Push Notifications key. EAS signs into your Apple Developer account and uploads the key. Enable the Push Notifications capability on the app target as well.

sections.heading: Step 3: Android (FCM)
sections.text:
1. Create a Firebase project, add an Android app with your package name, and download `google-services.json`.
2. Place it in the repo and point `android.googleServicesFile` at it in `app.config.ts`.
3. Run `npx eas-cli credentials`, choose Android, and upload the FCM v1 service-account key (with the Cloud Messaging API enabled).

`google-services.json` and any service-account key are secrets. Keep them out of version control.

sections.heading: Step 4: Build and test
sections.text:
A new build is required after wiring credentials. Then verify delivery directly through Expo Push using a token from `driver_push_tokens`:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"to":"ExponentPushToken[xxxx]","title":"Test","body":"Hello"}'
```

A delivered banner confirms credentials and the project id are correct. Then trigger a real event to confirm the backend path with `push_enabled` true.

sections.heading: Run on a Real Device
sections.text: A development build loads JavaScript from Metro on your computer. The device needs a path to Metro, and the app must be a development build, not Expo Go.

sections.heading: Android over USB
sections.text:
1. Enable Developer options and USB debugging on the phone, then connect it over USB and accept the authorization prompt.
2. Build and install onto the connected device (JDK 17 is required for the Android Gradle Plugin):

```bash
   export JAVA_HOME="$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)"
   npx expo run:android
   ```

3. Map the phone's `localhost:8081` to your computer's Metro so the app can reach the bundler:

```bash
   adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081
   ```

The `adb reverse` mapping is cleared whenever Metro or adb restarts. If the app suddenly stops loading with "No script URL provided", re-run `adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081` and reload.

sections.heading: Android over Wi-Fi
sections.text: Instead of USB, the dev client can reach Metro at your computer's LAN address (for example `http://192.168.1.50:8081`) as long as the phone and computer are on the same network. No cable is needed, but your computer must be running Metro.

sections.heading: iOS Simulator
sections.text:
```bash
npx expo run:ios
```

To target a specific simulator, boot it first and pass its name:

```bash
xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 15 Pro"
npx expo run:ios --device "iPhone 15 Pro"
```

sections.heading: Physical iPhone
sections.text:
A physical iPhone needs a development build signed with your Apple team and the device registered in your provisioning profile. EAS can manage this for you (see Build).

Device attestation cannot produce a real token on a simulator, so attestation-gated flows may fail there. Use a physical device to exercise attestation end to end.

sections.heading: Standalone (no computer)
sections.text: To run the app untethered, build a release variant. A release build bundles the JavaScript into the app, so it launches without Metro. See Build.

sections.heading: Mobile App Setup
sections.text: This guide gets the EVtivity mobile app running on your machine against a CSMS instance.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text:
- The latest LTS release of Node.js, and Git.
- A running EVtivity CSMS and its API URL.
- For Android: Android Studio with the SDK and platform tools, plus JDK 17 (the Android Gradle Plugin requires Java 17).
- For iOS: macOS with Xcode and the iOS Simulator.
- The Expo CLI is invoked with `npx expo` (no global install needed).

You cannot use the Expo Go app. EVtivity ships custom native modules (device attestation), so it needs a development build, not Expo Go.

sections.heading: Install
sections.text:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/EVtivity/evtivity-mobile-app.git
cd evtivity-mobile-app
npm install
```

sections.heading: Configure the environment
sections.text:
Create a `.env` file with the API URL of the CSMS the app should talk to:

```bash
EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://192.168.1.50:7102
ACTIVE_BRAND=default
```

- `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is baked into the bundle. Use a host the device can reach (a LAN IP for a physical device, not `localhost`).
- `ACTIVE_BRAND` selects which entry under `brands/` drives the app name, identifiers, and theme. See Configure Expo.

sections.heading: Run the development build
sections.text:
The first run compiles the native app and installs it on a simulator or device. After that, only JavaScript reloads through Metro.

On iOS (Simulator):

```bash
npx expo run:ios
```

On Android (note JDK 17):

```bash
export JAVA_HOME="$(/usr/libexec/java_home -v 17)"
npx expo run:android
```

If Metro is not already running, start it in a separate terminal:

```bash
npx expo start --dev-client
```

The app launches, connects to Metro, downloads the JavaScript bundle, and shows the login screen. Sign in with a driver account from your CSMS.

A development build loads JavaScript from Metro at launch, so your computer must be reachable. To run the app standalone, make a release build (see Build).

sections.heading: Next steps
sections.text:
- Configure Expo to set identifiers, icons, and brands.
- Run on a real device for USB and Wi-Fi testing.

sections.heading: Testing
sections.text: The app relies on static checks and on-device verification.

sections.heading: Typecheck and lint
sections.text:
Run both after a change. They catch the majority of issues before the app even loads.

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
npx eslint <changed-files>
```

The TypeScript config is strict (`exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`). Index access returns `T | undefined`, so read array and record values into a local with a fallback before using them.

sections.heading: On-device verification
sections.text:
Static checks do not catch layout, gesture, or native behavior. Reload the app on a simulator or device and exercise the change.

- Most edits hot-reload through Metro (shake the device or press reload).
- i18n and native config changes require a full relaunch (terminate and launch), not a Metro reload.
- Overlays (dialogs, sheets) must be verified on a real device or simulator, never assumed. The New Architecture has surprising behavior with the React Native `Modal`, which is why the app renders overlays in-tree.

sections.heading: What to check after a change
sections.text:
- The screen renders on both light and dark themes.
- Text contrast is correct on the branded backdrop and inside cards.
- Lists and details stay in sync after a mutation.
- Pull-to-refresh and any live-updating values behave.

When something behaves differently in a release build than in the Metro dev build, suspect native config: cleartext HTTP, attestation, or a value that is only present after a rebuild.

sections.heading: Next steps
sections.text:
- Run on a real device for the device and Metro connection workflow.
- Build to produce a standalone app for end-to-end testing.

sections.heading: White-labeling
sections.text:
The mobile app is built to be white-labeled. One codebase produces many branded apps: each charging network can publish the driver app under its own name, icon, colors, identifiers, and legal pages, pointing at its own CSMS. Nothing in the screens is hard-coded to "EVtivity"; everything brandable comes from a brand definition.

The app carries the same Business Source License 1.1 as the EVtivity CSMS, so free production use is limited to a single charging network. A single operator may build and publish one branded app for its own network at no cost. The "one codebase, many brands" capability is a build-time feature, not a grant to run apps for multiple independent networks for free: publishing or operating branded apps for more than one independent network as a service requires a commercial license. See Licensing below.

sections.heading: The brand model
sections.text:
Every brand is an entry in `brands/`. The active brand is chosen at build time by the `ACTIVE_BRAND` environment variable. A brand supplies:

- Identity: `name`, `slug`, `scheme`.
- Store identifiers: `iosBundleId`, `androidPackage`.
- Backend: `apiUrl` (the CSMS this brand talks to).
- Push: `easProjectId`.
- Legal: `termsUrl`, `privacyUrl`.
- Look: `colors` (light and dark), `icon`, `splash`, `adaptiveIcon`.
- Locales: the `languages` offered.

`app.config.ts` reads the active brand and assembles the Expo config from it: app name, icons, bundle id, package, ATS and cleartext exceptions, plugins, and `extra.eas.projectId`. The brand values are baked into the JavaScript bundle through `extra`, so screens read them at runtime through the config helpers.

sections.heading: How a network runs its own brand
sections.text:
A network operator runs three things: its own CSMS deployment, its own brand entry, and its own store listings. The flow from operator to driver:

Stand up a CSMS. The operator deploys its own EVtivity CSMS and configures branding in Settings (company name, logo, colors, legal pages). The CSMS serves the operator's drivers, stations, pricing, and payments.

Add a brand entry. In the app repo, add a brand under `brands/` with the operator's name, identifiers, theme, legal URLs, and `apiUrl` pointing at the operator's CSMS API.

Build the branded app. Set `ACTIVE_BRAND` to that brand and build. `app.config.ts` produces an app with the operator's name, icon, splash, colors, and bundle id, talking to the operator's backend.

Publish under the operator's accounts. Submit to the App Store and Google Play under the operator's developer accounts, using the brand's bundle id and package. Push credentials (APNs, FCM) belong to the operator too.

Drivers use their network's app. A driver installs the operator-branded app, which connects only to that operator's CSMS. Two operators run visually distinct apps, on separate backends, from the same source code.

sections.heading: Card verification return (Adyen)
sections.text:
With Adyen as the payment provider, 3D Secure sends the driver to the bank's page and back into the app. The CSMS accepts that return only for the app builds it knows. List every brand you publish in two CSMS settings:

| Setting | Brand value | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `mobile.app.urlSchemes` | `scheme`. iOS returns to `://payments/adyen`. | `["evtivity"]` |
| `mobile.app.androidPackageNames` | `androidPackage`. Android returns to `adyencheckout://`. | `["com.evtivity.driver"]` |

Both settings are JSON lists and have no dashboard field. Set them on Helm (`appSettings.mobile.app.urlSchemes` and `appSettings.mobile.app.androidPackageNames`), on CDK (`appSettings['mobile.app.urlSchemes']` and `appSettings['mobile.app.androidPackageNames']`), or with `PUT /v1/settings/:key`. A scheme must be lowercase and cannot be `http`, `https`, or `adyencheckout`. A brand missing from the lists cannot save an Adyen card that needs 3D Secure: the API answers 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. See Adyen.

Some branding is also served at runtime from the CSMS (`/v1/portal/branding`): the company name and logo can come from the operator's Settings, so a few visual details can change without an app release. Identifiers, icons, and store listings are build-time and per operator.

sections.heading: Theming
sections.text: The brand's `colors` feed the design system's light and dark palettes (the same tokens the components reference through NativeWind). Because components never hard-code colors, swapping the palette restyles the whole app. The branded backdrop and surfaces keep text contrast correct in both themes.

sections.heading: Licensing
sections.text:
The mobile app is licensed under the Business Source License 1.1, the same license as the EVtivity CSMS, so the production grant is the same: free use is limited to a single charging network.

- Permitted for free: building, publishing, and operating one branded driver app for your own single charging network, pointing at your own CSMS. Development, testing, demonstration, educational, and non-profit use are always permitted.
- Requires a commercial license: publishing or operating branded versions of the app for more than one independent charging network (white-label as a service, resale, or multi-tenant platforms). The "one codebase, many brands" capability is a build-time feature, not a grant to run apps for multiple networks for free.

The license converts to Apache 2.0 four years after each version is released. The full terms live in the app repo at LICENSE.md. For commercial licensing, contact evtivity@gmail.com.

Keep brand-specific secrets (push keys, service accounts, signing) in each operator's own accounts and out of version control. The repository holds brand configuration, not credentials.

sections.heading: Checklist for a new brand
sections.text:
- Brand entry in `brands/` with identity, identifiers, `apiUrl`, theme, and legal URLs.
- CSMS branding configured in the operator's Settings.
- With Adyen: the brand's `scheme` in `mobile.app.urlSchemes` and its `androidPackage` in `mobile.app.androidPackageNames` on the CSMS.
- EAS project id and push credentials under the operator's accounts.
- App Store and Google Play listings with the brand's identifiers.
- Icons and splash sized for both platforms.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Account page is the fourth tab in the Portal bottom navigation. It lists a row for each account-related setting. Each row opens its own page.

sections.heading: Personal Info
sections.text:
The Personal Info page holds your profile and display settings.

1. Tap Personal Info.
2. Edit any of the following fields:
   - First name and Last name
   - Email (shown only: ask the operator to change it)
   - Phone (used for SMS notifications and MFA)
   - Language (English, Deutsch, Español, 한국어, 简体中文, or 繁體中文)
   - Timezone (affects how timestamps are displayed)
   - Theme (Light or Dark)
   - Distance Unit (miles or km, affects vehicle range estimates and session summaries)
   - Show prices (Operator default, Including tax (gross), or Excluding tax (net))
3. Tap Save to apply changes. All fields persist in one request, and the language bundle reloads in place if you switched it.

When your account has a second factor, a new phone number needs a proof first: a code of your method or one of your passkeys. When you sign in with SMS codes, also tap Send Code to New Number and enter the code from the text message under Code Sent to the New Number. The number is saved only once confirmed. The mobile app cannot change the number of such an account and tells you to use the portal.

sections.heading: Billing Address
sections.text:
The Billing Address section on the Personal Info page holds the address printed on the invoices your fleet addresses to you. See Invoices.

1. Tap Personal Info.
2. In Billing Address, enter Name on Invoice, Street, City, State or Region, Postal Code, and Country. Leave Name on Invoice empty to use your first and last name.
3. Tap Save in the section.

When your fleet invoices your sessions to you and you have no billing address yet, the section shows "Your fleet invoices your sessions to you. Add your billing address so it appears on your invoices." Without an address, your invoices show your name and email. The operator can also edit the address, and the mobile app shows the same one.

sections.heading: Show prices
sections.text:
Show prices sets how the Portal shows charger prices and session costs:

- Including tax (gross) shows prices with tax added.
- Excluding tax (net) shows prices before tax.
- Operator default follows the operator's setting and names it, for example "Operator default (Including tax (gross))". New accounts start here.

You pay the same amount either way. The choice changes only how prices are shown. The same choice applies in the mobile app, because it is saved on your account.

sections.heading: Security
sections.text: The Security section lets you change your password and manage MFA, passkeys and security keys, and recovery codes.

sections.heading: Change Password
sections.text:
1. Tap Security.
2. Enter your current password.
3. Enter your new password.
4. Tap Change password.

sections.heading: Multi-Factor Authentication
sections.text: The Security section shows your current MFA status, your passkeys and security keys, and how many recovery codes are left. See Multi-Factor Authentication for setup, recovery codes and disabling MFA, and Passkeys and Security Keys for passkeys.

sections.heading: Notification Preferences
sections.text:
Control how you receive notifications from the charging network.

1. Tap Notifications.
2. Toggle Email notifications on or off.
3. Toggle SMS notifications on or off.
4. Tap Save to apply changes.

Notification preferences apply to session events (started, completed, idling, payment received) and system events (receipts, support case updates). Language, timezone, theme, and distance unit live under Personal Info, not here.

sections.heading: Invoices
sections.text: Tap Invoices to see your invoices and credit notes and download them as PDFs. See Invoices.

sections.heading: Favorites
sections.text: Save frequently used stations for quick access.

sections.heading: Add a Favorite
sections.text:
1. Navigate to a station detail page (via search or QR code).
2. Tap Add to Favorites above the Report Issue button.
3. A filled star icon appears next to the station ID.

sections.heading: View Favorites
sections.text: Tap the star icon in the Portal header (left of the notification bell) to open the Favorites page. The page lists your saved stations with EVSE counts.

sections.heading: Remove a Favorite
sections.text: On the Favorites page, tap the remove button on the station you want to unfavorite.

sections.heading: Notification Bell
sections.text:
The bell icon in the Portal header shows your unread notification count. Tap it to open the notification drawer, which slides up from the bottom of the screen and displays your notification history. Opening the drawer marks all notifications as read.

The unread count refreshes every 60 seconds.

sections.heading: Sign Out
sections.text: At the bottom of the Account page, tap Sign out to log out of the Portal.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Each row on the Account page opens its own page. Tap the back arrow to return.
- Payment Methods and Support Cases sections link to their respective full pages.
- Language changes take effect immediately across the entire Portal.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The Activity tab is the second item in the portal's bottom navigation (Home, Activity, Charge, Account). It shows your charging history organized by month with summary metrics and a session list.

sections.heading: Page Layout
sections.text: The page is organized top to bottom:

sections.heading: Monthly Statement Banner
sections.text: A card at the top linking to the itemized statement page for the selected month. Tap the banner or navigate directly to `/activity/statement?month=YYYY-MM` to open the statement.

sections.heading: Month Selector
sections.text: Left and right arrows with an uppercase month label (for example, JANUARY 2026). Tap the arrows to move between months. The selector wraps around - navigating past December moves to January of the next year, and navigating before January moves to December of the previous year.

sections.heading: Donut Chart
sections.text: A circular chart displaying the selected metric value in the center with an animated transition when switching metrics or months.

sections.heading: Metric Toggle
sections.text:
Three segments below the donut chart: Cost, Energy, and Distance. Tap a segment to switch the donut chart to that metric.

- Cost - total charging cost for the selected month, tax included, formatted as currency
- Energy - total energy consumed in kWh
- Distance - estimated miles driven, calculated from energy using your vehicle's efficiency (mi/kWh)

If you have not added a vehicle, the Distance metric uses a default efficiency of 3.5 mi/kWh. See Vehicles for details on how miles are calculated.

sections.heading: Session List
sections.text:
Each row in the session list shows:

- Status dot - color-coded by session status
- Station ID - the identifier of the station used
- Site name - the location name
- Date and time - when the session occurred
- Energy - total kWh delivered
- Cost - total session cost, followed by "incl. tax" when the session's tariff has tax

Tap any session row to view the full session detail page.

sections.heading: Session Status Dots
sections.text:
The colored dot on each session row indicates its status:

| Color  | Status    |
|--------|-----------|
| Green  | Active    |
| Gray   | Completed |
| Red    | Failed    |
| Amber  | Pending   |

sections.heading: Monthly Statement
sections.text:
The Monthly Statement provides an itemized breakdown of all sessions for the selected month. Access it from the banner card on the Activity page.

The statement table includes the following columns:

- Date - session date and time
- Location - site name where the session occurred
- Energy - kWh delivered during the session
- Duration - how long the session lasted
- Miles - estimated miles driven (based on vehicle efficiency)
- Cost - total cost of the session. The column reads Cost (incl. tax) when a session cost includes tax.

A totals row at the bottom sums each column for the month. Sessions your fleet pays on account show "Billed to" and the fleet name instead of a cost and are left out of the total. Sessions billed in an earlier currency are left out of the total, and a note below the table counts them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Activity data is only available for authenticated drivers. Guest sessions do not appear here.
- Distance calculations depend on your vehicle efficiency setting. See Vehicles.
- Sessions are grouped by the month in which they started, in your timezone.
- A faulted or failed session at no cost shows Not Charged.
- The Activity page loads session data for the selected month on each navigation.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Authenticated drivers can start charging sessions by scanning a QR code at a station or by searching for stations in the Portal. This guide covers both entry points, the station detail page, and the active session experience.

sections.heading: QR Code Flow
sections.text:
Every charging station has a QR code that links to the Portal.

1. Scan the QR code with your phone camera. The URL format is `/charge/:stationId/:evseId` (specific connector) or `/charge/:stationId` (station level).
2. If you are logged in, the Portal redirects you to the authenticated charging page at `/start/:stationId`. If a specific connector was in the QR code, it is preselected.
3. If you are not logged in, you see the guest landing page. Tap Sign In to log in and continue with authenticated charging, or charge as a guest (see Guest Charging).

sections.heading: Search for a Station
sections.text:
1. Open the Portal and tap the Charge tab in the bottom navigation.
2. The search page detects your location via browser geolocation. Nearby stations within 10 miles are displayed automatically.
3. Use the search bar to find stations by name, ID, or address.
4. Tap a station to open the station detail page.

If location access is denied, a banner prompts you to enable location services. You can still search by name or address.

Nearby station results are cached in localStorage for 24 hours.

sections.heading: Station Detail Page
sections.text: The station detail page at `/start/:stationId` shows everything you need to start a session.

sections.heading: Station Information
sections.text:
- Station ID and site name - displayed at the top of the page
- Online/offline status - indicator showing whether the station is communicating with the CSMS
- Address - tap to view the Location Detail page with map and popular times
- Site contact information - shown when the operator marks the contact as public
- Favorites star - tap to add or remove the station from your Favorites
- Report Issue - link to create a support case about this station

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.text:
The pricing section displays the resolved tariff for your account. This is the price the operator has assigned based on your driver group or the default tariff. Pricing components may include per-kWh rates, per-minute rates, flat fees, or a combination.

Prices are shown excluding or including tax, depending on your Show prices choice in Account settings or, until you choose, the operator default. When the tariff has tax, a note below the price says which one you see, for example "Prices include 19% tax" or "Prices exclude 19% tax, which is added to the amount charged". Prices show 2 to 4 decimals, so a price such as 0.357 per kWh is not rounded. The pricing section appears once the Portal knows which display applies.

When the resolved tariff has time-of-day or other restrictions, a one-line summary appears below the rate, for example "Mon, Tue, Wed 09:00-17:00" or "Holiday rate". For a time or day restriction, the summary names the timezone of the time window, for example "Times in Europe/Berlin". If the site is in free vend mode, the section shows a Free charging badge instead of a rate.

When the price can change during the session, a note says so: "The price can change during the session (time of day, day or energy charged)." This happens when the operator bills each tariff change separately and the station has tariffs for other times or amounts of energy.

A tariff shows as free when all its prices are zero, whatever its tax rate.

sections.heading: EVSE Grid
sections.text:
The EVSE grid shows all connectors at the station. Each tile displays:

- Connector type - CCS2, CHAdeMO, Type 2, J1772, etc.
- Power rating - maximum power output in kW
- Amperage - maximum current in amps
- Port number - the physical port identifier on the station
- Status badge - color-coded availability status

Connector Status Colors

| Status       | Color  | Meaning                                    |
|--------------|--------|--------------------------------------------|
| Available    | Green  | Ready for use, no cable detected           |
| Occupied     | Blue   | Active charging session in progress        |
| Preparing    | Cyan   | Cable connected, waiting for authorization |
| EV Connected | Cyan   | Cable connected to the vehicle             |
| Reserved     | Orange | Held by a reservation until the time shown |
| Suspended    | Yellow | Session paused by vehicle or station       |
| Faulted      | Red    | Hardware or communication error            |
| Unavailable  | Red    | Taken out of service by operator           |

Station Unavailable

When the whole station is unavailable, the page shows "This station is unavailable right now. Try another station." and no connector tile can be selected. This happens when the operator disabled the station, a firmware install is running or failed, or the station reports a fault. A single faulted connector blocks only that connector.

sections.heading: Select a Connector
sections.text:
1. On the station detail page, tap an available connector tile.
2. Only connectors with a startable status (available, occupied, preparing, or ev_connected) can be selected. A connector you reserved can also be selected. A connector reserved by another driver cannot. No connector can be selected while the station is unavailable.
3. The selected connector is highlighted with a border.

sections.heading: Pre-Start Status Check
sections.text:
Before starting, the Portal sends a TriggerMessage to the station to request a fresh StatusNotification.

1. The system triggers a status refresh from the station.
2. If the connector status is available (no cable detected), a warning dialog asks you to plug in your EV before proceeding. You can dismiss the warning and start anyway.
3. If the connector is ready (cable connected), the session starts immediately.

This check prevents failed start attempts when the cable is not plugged in.

On an OCPP 2.1 station, you can also start from the Portal when your cable is already plugged in and the station is waiting for authorization.

sections.heading: Select a Payment Method
sections.text:
1. After selecting a connector, your default payment method is shown.
2. To use a different card, tap the payment method selector dropdown and choose from your saved cards.
3. If you have no payment method on file and the tariff is not free, you must add one before starting. See Payment Methods. You also need one when the current tariff is free but a paid tariff can apply later in the session.

sections.heading: Charge on Account
sections.text: If your fleet bills your sessions on account, the station page shows Billed to and your fleet in place of the payment methods. You start without a card, no amount is held, and your fleet pays the session on its invoice. At a free vend site nothing is billed. See Fleets. When your fleet invoices each member, the page shows "Billed to you via" and your fleet, and the session goes on your monthly invoice. See Invoices.

sections.heading: Start Charging
sections.text:
1. Tap Start Charging.
2. The Portal sends a `RequestStartTransaction` command to the station.
3. The session detail page opens automatically.

sections.heading: Start on Your Reservation
sections.text: When you hold a reservation on the station, start as usual on the reserved connector. The session is linked to your reservation, so no no-show fee applies. Starting with the RFID card you last used works the same way. Another driver cannot use your reservation: if someone else starts on the connector, you are notified and no no-show fee applies.

sections.heading: Reserve a Connector
sections.text:
When the operator has turned on reservations, you can hold a connector before you arrive.

1. Tap the Reserve tab, then New reservation.
2. Search for the station and select it.
3. Optionally select a connector, then set Starts at and Expires at.
4. Tap Reserve Connector.

A reservation that starts now is sent to the station, and the Portal waits for the station to confirm the hold. If the station refuses or does not answer, the Portal shows an error and the reservation is cancelled with no fee. A reservation that starts later is sent to the station at its start time.

A no-show fee applies only when the station confirmed the hold, you did not charge, and the station stayed available. If the station goes offline or reports a fault during your reservation, the reservation is cancelled, no fee is charged, and you get a notification. A cancellation fee applies only when you cancel inside the operator's cancellation window. The Portal shows the no-show fee before you reserve, and the cancellation policy on the reservation.

sections.heading: Active Session
sections.text:
After starting, the Portal shows the session detail page with live charging data:

- Energy - kWh delivered so far, updating in real time
- Estimated cost - running cost based on the tariff and energy consumed
- Duration timer - elapsed time since the session started
- Stop Charging button - tap to end the session early

The session detail page updates via polling to show the latest data from the station. The polling interval is a few seconds during active charging.

When the session completes (either by tapping Stop or when the vehicle stops drawing power), the page shows the final session summary with total energy, duration, and cost.

When the station refuses the stop, the page shows "The station rejected the stop request. The session is still charging." When the station is offline, the page reports that too, and the session keeps running until the station ends it.

sections.heading: Ghost Transaction Recovery
sections.text:
If the station rejects the start command because it already has an active transaction the CSMS does not know about, the system automatically:

1. Stops the unknown transaction on the station.
2. Retries the start command.
3. If the retry succeeds, charging begins normally.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Charging sessions require a verified email and a valid payment method, unless the tariff is free and no paid tariff can apply later in the session.
- A driver whose fleet bills on account needs no payment method.
- The Portal supports OCPP 1.6, 2.0.1 and 2.1 stations.
- Live session data (energy, cost, duration) updates in real time via polling.
- If a session fails to start, the Portal displays an error message with the reason from the station.
- A start request at an unavailable station returns `409 STATION_UNAVAILABLE`.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Drivers can save favorite stations for quick access. The Favorites page is accessible from the star icon in the portal header, located to the left of the notification bell.

sections.heading: Adding a Favorite
sections.text:
To add a station to your favorites:

1. Open the Station Detail page for any charging station.
2. Tap the star icon next to the station ID, or tap the Add to Favorites button.
3. The star icon fills in to confirm the station was saved.

Favorited stations show a filled star icon on the Station Detail page. Stations that have not been favorited show an outlined star.

sections.heading: Favorites Page
sections.text:
The Favorites page lists all saved stations as cards. Each card displays the following information:

- Station name - the operator-assigned station identifier
- Site name - the site where the station is located
- Address - full street address of the site
- EVSE count - total number of connectors at the station
- Available count - how many connectors are currently available for charging
- Connector types - the connector standards supported (CCS2, CHAdeMO, Type 2, etc.)

sections.heading: Status Indicators
sections.text:
Each station card shows an online or offline status indicator:

- Green dot - the station is online and communicating with the CSMS
- Gray dot - the station is offline or not responding

These indicators update each time you open the Favorites page.

sections.heading: Removing a Favorite
sections.text:
To remove a station from your favorites:

1. Open the Favorites page from the star icon in the portal header.
2. Tap the trash icon on the station card you want to remove.
3. The station is removed from the list immediately.

You can also unfavorite a station by tapping the filled star icon on the Station Detail page.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
- Favorites are tied to your driver account and persist across devices.
- The Favorites page is only available to authenticated drivers.
- If a station is taken offline or removed by the operator, it still appears in your favorites with an offline indicator.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Guest charging lets drivers use a charging station without creating a Portal account. Drivers scan a QR code, see pricing, pay with a credit card (if required), and monitor the session on a temporary tracking page.

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.text:
1. A driver scans the QR code on a charging station.
2. The Portal opens the guest landing page showing station info, connector details, and pricing.
3. If the tariff is free, the driver taps Start Charging directly.
4. If the tariff requires payment, the driver taps Pay with card to proceed to checkout.
5. The session starts and the driver monitors progress on a temporary session page.

sections.heading: Guest Landing Page
sections.text: The QR code URL follows the format `/charge/:stationId/:evseId` (specific connector) or `/charge/:stationId` (station level).

sections.heading: Dynamic QR Codes
sections.text:
Some OCPP 2.1 stations show a QR code on their display that changes over time instead of a printed one. The code holds a one-time password that is valid only for a short period, so a photo or copy of the code expires. The operator turns this on per station (see Stations).

When a driver scans a dynamic QR code, the portal opens `/qr/...` and checks the password:

- Valid code: the portal continues to the landing page of that connector, the same page a static QR code opens.
- Expired or invalid code: the portal shows QR Code Not Valid and does not start a session. Scan the QR code shown on the station again.

A valid scan gives the browser a scan token for that connector, valid for 10 minutes. At a station with dynamic QR codes, a guest start needs it: a printed or bookmarked `/charge/...` link, or a start more than 10 minutes after the scan, is refused with "Scan the QR code shown on the charger to start charging." (`QR_SCAN_REQUIRED`). Scan the code on the charger again.

If the station let the driver enter a maximum cost, energy, or time before it showed the code, the code URL carries them as `maxcost`, `maxenergy` (Wh), and `maxtime` (seconds). They limit the session the same way for static and dynamic QR codes.

sections.heading: Single Connector Landing (/charge/:stationId/:evseId)
sections.text:
This page shows the details for a specific connector:

- Station name - the operator-assigned station identifier
- Connector type - CCS2, CHAdeMO, Type 2, or other standard
- Power rating - maximum output in kW
- Status badge - current connector availability
- Pricing breakdown - tariff components (per-kWh, per-minute, flat fee, etc.). Guests see prices excluding or including tax as the operator's price display setting sets, with a note naming the tax rate.

Two buttons appear at the bottom:

- Pay with card - proceed to the card checkout for guest charging
- Sign In - redirect to the login page for authenticated charging with an account

If the driver is already logged in, the page redirects automatically to the authenticated charging flow at `/start/:stationId`.

sections.heading: Station Landing (/charge/:stationId)
sections.text:
This page shows all EVSEs at the station in a grid layout. Each tile displays the connector type, power rating, and current status. Tap an available connector to navigate to the single connector landing page.

Connectors that are faulted or unavailable are shown but cannot be selected.

When the whole station is unavailable (disabled by the operator, installing firmware, failed firmware install, or a station-level fault), both landing pages show "This station is unavailable right now. Try another station." and no connector can be selected. A guest start request at that station returns `409 STATION_UNAVAILABLE`.

sections.heading: Free Stations
sections.text:
Some stations are configured for free charging. On these stations:

1. The guest landing page shows Free pricing with no cost components.
2. No credit card is required.
3. The Pay with card button is replaced with Start Charging.
4. Tap Start Charging to begin the session immediately without entering payment details.

sections.heading: Card Checkout
sections.text:
When the tariff requires payment:

1. Tap Pay with card on the guest landing page.
2. The Guest Checkout page opens with the card form of the operator's payment provider (Stripe or Adyen). Card data goes straight to the provider.
3. Enter your credit or debit card number, expiration date, and CVC.
4. Optionally enter your email address in Email (for receipt) to receive a receipt.
5. The pre-authorization amount is displayed above the button: "A hold of ... will be placed on your card. You will only be charged for the energy used."
6. Tap Start Charging to authorize the hold and begin the session.

The system places a pre-authorization hold on your card. The final charge is captured when the session ends based on actual energy consumed and time elapsed. If the final amount is less than the hold, the difference is released. A guest has no saved card, so a cost above the hold is not charged. When the station's QR code sets a maximum cost below the hold, that maximum is the limit instead: the session stops there and you are charged no more than it.

If the card is refused, the session does not start and the page shows the reason, for example "Your card was declined. Try a different card." Try another card.

sections.heading: Start Protection
sections.text:
Every guest start, free or paid, is checked before the station is asked to start:

- reCAPTCHA: when the operator turns reCAPTCHA on, the guest start needs a passing reCAPTCHA score, as the sign-in pages do.
- Starts per address: one client IP address can start at most Guest Starts per IP per Hour guest sessions in an hour (default 30).
- Declined cards per address: after Declined Cards per IP per Hour declined cards from one IP address in an hour (default 5), that address can place no new payment hold.

Over a limit, the start returns `RATE_LIMITED`. The operator sets both limits under Settings > Integrations & Features > Guest Charging, where 0 means no limit. They apply only when the server knows the guest's real IP address: behind a load balancer or ingress, set `TRUST_PROXY` (see Environment Variables). When the API is reached directly on a public address, they apply as is.

sections.heading: Card Verification (3D Secure)
sections.text:
With Adyen, your bank can ask you to confirm the payment. The page shows "Complete the verification from your bank to continue." and opens your bank's page. After you confirm, the browser returns to the Card Verification page (`/payments/return`), which finishes the verification, starts the session, and opens the session tracking page. If the card is refused or the verification fails, the session does not start, no money stays held, and the page shows the reason with View charging session.

With Stripe, guest checkout has no verification step: a card that requires 3D Secure is declined, so use another card.

sections.heading: Test Mode
sections.text: When the operator runs the test payment provider, the checkout shows "Test mode, no real money. Pick a test card." and a Test card list instead of card fields. See Test Payment Provider.

sections.heading: Session Tracking
sections.text:
After starting, you are redirected to a session tracking page at `/guest-session/:sessionToken`.

The session token is stored in the URL. You do not need an account to access this page - anyone with the URL can view the session status. Bookmark the page or keep the browser tab open to monitor your session.

The page shows:

- Session status - current state of the charging session
- Live stats - duration, energy delivered, and estimated cost (updates every 5 seconds). The cost includes tax and reads Estimated cost (incl. tax), then Total cost (incl. tax) when the session ends, when the tariff has tax.
- Power chart - real-time power output graph (updates every 10 seconds)
- Stop Charging - tap to end the session early

sections.heading: Session Statuses
sections.text:
